title: Providing HIV and AIDS education for illiterate women through community learning centres (CLCs)

  4. Revision and production of the learning material and its dissemination to other 80 groups through CLCs

  5. Organization of literacy classes (ca 20 women/class) to 80 groups through CLCs

  8. Monitoring, follow-up, evaluation and reporting of the project
    (December 2011)

title: 64-11204012-KAT (Culture) Enhancing national capacities for the effective implementation of the World Heritage Convention 1-4
description:
JUSTIFICATION
1. Regular monitoring need for Nepal's WH properties is reflected in frequent requests for interventions/changes related to properties
2. Need to monitor the implementation of the IMP for Kathmandu Valley and its possible review to tackle emerging challenges, including disaster risk reduction and tourism initiatives for sustainable heritage management;
3. Need to increase the awareness/participation of communities in heritage protection to address challenges of living with and around WH properties, targeting members of communities who are unacquainted or not well-informed of the opportunities, processes and protection needs of the properties as community assets
4. Need to assist the national authorities in the process of nominating new sites for inclusion in the World Heritage List
5. Little understanding of the role of cultural heritage as a contributor to the sustainable development of local communities

MODALITIES
1. Technical assistance in monitoring and assessment study
2. Capacity building and awareness raising workshops
3. Exploring extra-budgetary funding for
3.a Integrating disaster risk reduction strategies in management plans and its implementation
3.b Up scaling self-sustaining initiatives with community
3.b.1 Survey to review Manual for traditional home-owners for Kathmandu Valley and possible new edition
3.b.2 Exploring the potential of heritage to contribute to sustainable development
3.c Establishing coherent information /knowledge management system (for Lumbini in view of establishing documentation centre)
4. Strengthening partnership with local municipal offices, among others for promoting the application of UNESCO Recommendation on Historic Urban Landscape (HUL), especially in Kathmandu Valley
5. Strengthening inter-ministerial coordination to enhance understanding of and ensure support for WH protection at different levels
6. Cluster and regional exchanges for learning from international experiences
7. Leaflet Publication promoting World Heritage properties in Nepal and re-production of translated operational guidelines in Nepali
8. Advocating for Nepal's possible accession to Hague Convention and its two protocols

TARGET GROUPS
• Policy makers
• Site managers
• Community at large/ civil society and community leaders

RISK
• Possible interventions impacting the OUV of the World Heritage properties
• Loosening of credibility of UNESCO's action in the field

title: Franchising Skill Phase 3
description:
Provide training to franchisees on conducting RMAs, conduct/commission market surveys in/out of country, establish linkages with employment-supportive entities, conduct familiarization meetings/workshops with private sector associations, Chamber of Commerce, Implement training events with high employment potential.

Develop and update training manuals in line with NSTB skill standards. Develop curriculum guides and training manuals based on OSS Level 1 and elementary level.Support and encourgae trainees to take skill tests after completion of training.

Ensure that the technical training is conducted according to NSTB standards. Develop and implement psycho-social counselling strategy for all employment markets (Overseas, Indian and Nepalese market). Provide regular training and orientation to F-SKILL staff on PSA appraoch and modality. Implement HIV/AIDS awareness raising and sensitization packages for all training

Establish linkages with financial institutions. Disseminate the F-SKILL working modality. Conduct regular dialouge and follow up with potential loan providers. Support franchisees in establishing linkages with loan providers.

Develop and implement strategy to increase efficiency in monitoring. Define criteria to decide on whether a trade/occupations are replicable and follow agreed procedure.

Develop and implement marketing and acquisition strategy. Develop a roster of potential donors. Enter a regular dialogue with potential donors on employment oriented skills development and F-SKILL services. Use different means of regularly communicating F-SKILL developments and achievements. Develop alternative financing/pricing startegy (different from that of SDC).

Clearly communicate the added value the EF provides to donors and communicate it. Maintain regular dialogue through different means with donors and other potential contributors to the EF on employment-oriented skills training, policy etc. Support F-SKILL Pvt. Ltd in their efforts to facilitate loan access for course graduates.

GoN will be invited and encourged to take a lead role on the EF steering committee. EF enters maintains dialogue with Government of Nepal on employment oriented skills training, policy and related matters.

title: Partnerships: Research and Analytical -INTERNATIONAL CRISIS GROUP
description: The Partnerships: Research and Analytical initiative consolidates eight new and existing agreements that support and enhance strategic partnerships with leading research institutions in fragility, peace, conflict and development issues. The partnership will: ensure continued access to international cutting edge research, analysis and intellectual policy expertise ; ability to draw on international best practice and lessons learned from fragile, complex and conflict affected environments; provide an opportunity to input and steer direction at international policy discussion level; access to international products and materials including guidance notes, analysis and toolkits. This initiative contributes to two of the Crisis Prevention, Stabilisation and Recovery (CPSR) Group's objectives: international and whole of government engagement by leveraging best practice and analysis for the  Australia aid program from strategic partnerships; and strategic advice guidance that draws on cross-Agency experience, international analysis and lessons learned from fragile, complex and conflict affected areas. The total value of this initiative is $11.9 million over 8 years, starting 2008-09.
funding_source: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
borrower: Ministry of Home Affairs
source: MoF DFMIS (Ministry of Finance - Development Finance Information Management System)

title: Isolated Water Supply System for Urban Poor Communities in Kathmandu Valley
description:
• Tokha Integrated Water and Sanitation intervention to ensure right of low income consumers to safe drinking water and a comprehensive sanitation master plan for planned sanitary intervention;
  • Water Bottling System for affordable drinking water access tp urban poor communities of Koteshwor and Chyasal;
  • Rehabilitation and Conservation of Traditional Water Sources and Harvesting Rain water;
  • Advocacy and Network on "Low Income Consumer Support" for affordable water supply.
borrower: Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport
source: MoF DFMIS (Ministry of Finance - Development Finance Information Management System)

title: Provision of Total Coverage of Safe Drinking Water and Sustainable Sanitation Facilities in Urban Poor Communities in Hetauda Municipality
description:
• Institutional and local level training;
  • Campaign for sanitation coverage;
  • Pro poor financing mechanism;
  • Community managed water supply system.
borrower: Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport
source: MoF DFMIS (Ministry of Finance - Development Finance Information Management System)

title: Cities and Climate Change Initiatives

title: NPLJ80: HIV Prevention, Care and Treatment for Female Injecting Drug Users, Female Prisoners and Women living with HIV and AIDS in Nepal
description:
·         Conduct rapid situation assessments needs analysis of female injecting drug users& female prisoners in specific locations, using existing secondary data, supplemented by second generation surveillance surveys.
·         Conduct operational research on drug use &sexual networks, & HIV risk behaviours.
·         Carry-out studies on lessons learned & best practices.
·         Conduct Epidemiological assessment in Prison Settings
·         Develop gender and culture sensitive advocacy and communication materials.
·         Promote gender & culture sensitive & rights-based programme approaches among govt. and civil society service providers.
·         Advocate with policy makersfor recognition of the need to establish female-specific interventions for injecting drug users and in prison settings.
·         Form self-help groups among female injecting drug users, prisoners and other HIV positive women.
·         Establish new drop-in-centre/s for PHC, sexual & reproductive health etc & continuation of the existing sites
·         Modify and continuation of the existing centres for the provision of HIV services
·         Conduct training and skills-needs assessment among existing and potential service providers
·         Develop gender sensitive training materials and manuals, locally adapted to specific social and cultural contexts.
·         Develop skills, including for peer educators, in specific technical areas (e.g., needle and syringe prog., condom promotion, HIV counselling, referral to other services).
·         Conduct training of peer educators on HIV and STI prevention, early detection and treatment measures.
·         Develop & distribute gender and culture sensitive training &other informa.materials/manuals.
·         Establish drop-in-centres
·         Develop and maintain referral mechanism
·         Support existing VCT centres or establish new centre.
·         Organise sensitisation programme for the national-level decision makers.
·         Develop &deliver gender sensitive training & other information materials/manuals as well as adapt in local context.
·         Conduct training of prison-based peer educators.
·         Provide comprehensive HIV prevention, treatment and care services.
·         Organise public events to increase public exposure of the forum &communicate effectively on the stated goals of the forum.
·         Provide strategic support to network as and when required, in its dealings with Govt.departments and other stakeholders.
·         Establish treatment and care centers for women living with HIV and AIDS
·         Support for participation at the national and international conferences
·         Document the impact of project on ground.

title: South Asia Water Initiative (SAWI)
description: The South Asia Water Initiative (SAWI) aims to promote regional cooperation in the sustainable management of the water resources of the Himalayan rivers to address the challenges of development and climate change.  The program will be structured around five key focus areas: (1) Ganges Basin, (2) Brahmaputra Basin, (3) Indus Basin, (4) Sundarbans Landscape, and (5) Regional Cooperation. To promote more effective and cooperative water resources management, SAWI will facilitate multi-stakeholder dialogue and policy deliberation; enhance knowledge and capacity on issues of regional, and in particular trans-boundary water resources management and climate adaptation; and promote cooperative actions such as policy reforms, institutional development, and investment in water resources management. The total value of this multi-country initiative is $9.0 million over 5 years, starting 2008-09.

title: International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF) South Asia Strategic Plan 2010-2015
description:
This initiative supports the International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF) South Asia Strategic Plan 2010-2015 and forms part of the Government's commitment to advance Millennium Development Goal (MDG) 5 (improve maternal health) in South Asia. The South Asia region has the highest rates of maternal and neonatal deaths and unmet demand for contraception in the Asia-Pacific. The funding of this initiative helps reduce maternal deaths in South Asia by improving equitable access for underserved groups to a range of reproductive health services and education including family planning. These goals are met by IPPF's South Asia Strategic Plan which focuses on 4 priority areas: 1) ensuring young people have access and rights to services and education; 2) reducing social, cultural and economic barriers that impede access; 3) HIV/AIDS prevention and care; and 4) reducing unsafe abortion. The total value of this multi-country initiative is up to $11 million over 3 years, starting 2010-11.

description: After languishing in refugee camps in eastern Nepal for 18 years, 108,000 registered Bhutanese refugees became eligible for third country resettlement in late 2007 due to the concerted efforts of a Core Group of resettlement countries, UNHCR and the Government of Nepal.  IOM assists in the resettlement of Bhutanese refugees from Nepal to the United States (and other countries) by 1) interviewing refugees and completing US Government forms; 2) conducting health assessments; 3) providing cultural orientation courses and 4) organizing transportation for refugees from the camps in eastern Nepal to their final destination in the United States.

title: Harmonization of Protocols for Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Treatment of the Bhutanese Refugees in Nepal (HAPT

Currently TB screening and treatment protocol implemented in the camps differs from the protocol of the resettlement countries. The purpose of this project is to ensure that the refugees who apply for resettlement and those who have not yet entered resettlement programmes receive the same effective TB diagnosis and treatment.

title: Trafficking Risk Reduction in Nepal (TRRIN)
description:
Lack of economic opportunities is one of the major factors driving people to migrate and giving traffickers the opportunity to lure potential victims. In cooperation with the Government of Nepal, NGOs and private sector businesses, IOM provides economic rehabilitation to returned victims and potential victims of trafficking through skills training, job placement and micro-enterprise setup.

NGOs are responsible for psychosocial counseling of the beneficiaries and supporting them in day to day management of their Micro-enterprises. The corporate houses extend business opportunities / franchisees to the beneficiaries and assist them by providing – business specific training, market linkages, skils training and job placements. The Government extends legal and infrastructural support to the initiatives. In addition to the financial inputs IOM is involved in the overall planning and coordination among various stakeholders, including Implementation and monitoring of all the project activities.

title: Exploring Livelihood Options for Trafficked Women in Nepal (LOPS)
description: To date there has been little research on post trafficking livelihoods or how the issues raised by trafficking intersect with development agendas. IOM in collaboration with Newcastle University, UK and the Non Governmental Organization “Shakti Samuha” is undertaking a research to explore the situation of returnee trafficked women. A key aspect of this research is to gain knowledge that is grounded in the actual experiences of the Nepalese trafficked returnee women themselves and how returnee livelihoods intersect with sexuality and citizenship. Furthermore project facilitates the current debates on the citizenship in the Constitution writing process through ongoing dialogue with relevant subject committees of the Constituent Assembly and Women’s Caucus of the legislative parliament.

title: Fairness and Efficiency in Reparations to Conflict-Affected Persons (FERC)
description: Over 14,000 people lost their lives and thousands more were the victims of gross human rights violations during the ten-year conflict which began in 1996 and ended with the signing of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement in 2006. IOM Nepal in partnership with OHCHR-Nepal is working with the Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction (MoPR) to develop and implement a comprehensive reparation policy in line with international human rights and humanitarian law standards.  In addition to developing reparations policy, the project will increase the capacity of relevant government agencies including MoPR as well as TRC and COI-D to develop and implement the needed procedures, processes and guidelines including a database essential for the successful implementation of a reparations program.

Design and conduct orientation to parents on child growth, development and benefits of CDC,Educate adolescents on their self protection and mechanism of complain process
Form saving groups
 
Design & conduct orientation on the importance of growth monitoring, conduct Monthly growth monitoring, Demonstrate and practicum on the preparation of jaulo and sorbottam pitho
 
Develop Work Plan with CMC, Design and conduct orientation on the basics of psychosocial support to Social Mobiliser, Peer group education on reproductive health and gender-based issues (e.g. violence etc.),Provide individual counselling, Refer cases to CMC for individual counselling, Supervision / follow-up of Counselling 
 
Design & Conduct orientation on the needs and benefits of safe drinking water and sanitation, Negotiate and sign MOU between the project and kiln owners for establishing water supply system in CDC
 

Organize workshops / meetings for developing the Code of conduct

title: The Sushma Koirala Memorial Hospital (SKMH) Project
description:
1. Create awareness of the services offered by the SKMH to encourage referrals ( particularly of difficult cases) by other hospital, surgeons, line agencies, NGO’s and health services providers.
  2. Expand the treatment of burns to include the whole spectrum of burns, post-burns contracture and defect wounds.

 

  • Conducts burn prevention campaigns.
  • Raise awareness of burns, the risks to women and children from cooking fires and kerosene stoves and how to prevent/ treat burns and expand the activities in this area to reduce the risks.
  • Expand fee-based cosmetic surgery services (not to exceed more than 10% of the total plastic, reconstructive and general surgery services) to generate more income to cover hospital-running expenses.
  • Expand fee-based emergency services for tourists (not to exceed more than 10% of the total of total plastic, reconstructive and general surgery services to generate more income to cover hospital - running expenses.
  • Formulate a human resource development plan including internal and external training and career opportunities.
  • Formulate a Gender Equity Policy.

title: Support and Protection for Street Children and Vulnerable Families of Nepal
description:
• Financial Support: As per SWC contract.
  • Technical Support: As per need
  • Training:

    Training for the Team of Educators and Social Workers

    The team of educators and social workers of VOC is highly motivated and all possess a great sensitivity to the problems of these children. Follow-ups and training sessions have allowed to evaluate their performance level, as well as to develop their capabilities and desire to progress.

     

    Street children project

    Several training sessions will be conducted either by external organizations or by EED. It aims at strengthening the capacity of VOC's educators, social workers and managers. The trainings topics could cover child development, child sexual abuse, language development, computer and language skills, etc.

    Prevention project

    The FDP approach has been successfully implemented in countries such as Cambodia and Philippines, but is quite new to Nepal. This new approach is being introduced by VOC, and hence, the staff from VOC will need to be trained on this new methodology.

 

  • Followup, Supervision and Monitoring: As per the provision in the agreement.

title: Save the Children Strategic Framework for Cooperation 2010 -2012
description:
Education: The focus of the education program is to reach the most marginalized communities. High priority is given to achieve universal primary education with a focus on gender parity and ensuring access to quality learning opportunities to all with a focus on girls and marginalized groups.

Child Protection: All vulnerable and survivor children will benefit from advocacy and capacity building of law implementing agencies program conducted at the national level. While the focused program to be implemented in the Mid and Far Western regions will particularly reach to the following children:

  • 30,000 vulnerable children including orphans, Badi, and socially and economically poor;
  • 5,000 survivors of violence;
  • 6,000 conflict affected children; and 5,000 women vulnerable to Chhaupadi.

Child rights: The primary beneficiaries of the project are children up to age of 18 years. SCNN ensures that no children are discriminated however; SCNN will focus its target to children who are from most marginalized and disadvantaged population, including promoting girls participation. The secondary target group of this component of the project are:

 

  • The Ministry of Women, Children and Social Welfare and the focal points on child rights implementation
  • The networks for child rights and participation
  • The child clubs and their networks
  • The National Human Rights Commission and any other HR monitoring bodies
  • National Non Governmental Organizations
borrower: Ministry of Women, Children and Senior Citizens
source: MoF DFMIS (Ministry of Finance - Development Finance Information Management System)

title: Rehalibitation of Critical Trail Bridges
description:
The proposed fund shall be utilised to procure the required steel parts including steel decks, anchorage parts, gabion mesh etc. required to rehabilitate the ‘critical’ trail bridges. SDC will procure the materials through a local bidding procedure and hand over the materials to the respective District Development Committees (DDC). The Trail Bridge Support Unit managed by Helvetas shall provide all the required technical and administrative support to SDC.

 

Districts are the main implementers at the operational level. Once they receive the steel parts from SDC, they shall allocate adequate budget for labour and other materials such as cement, sand and aggregate. It is also the responsibility of the DDC to organise the contribution from communities wherever applicable. All other approaches concerning social inclusion, transparency and governance, conflict sensitivity, insurance of labour, timely payments, steering, monitoring etc will be applied as usual

title: South Asia Food and Nutrition Security Initiative (SAFNSI)
description: South Asia Food and Nutrition Security Initiative (SAFANSI) forms part of the Government's commitment to advance Millennium Development Goals (MDG) in South Asia: MDG 1C reduce hunger; MDG 4 reduce child deaths; and MDG 5 improve maternal health. Malnutrition's most devastating impact is on foetal growth, and during the first two years of a child's life. Malnutrition accounts for up to 40% of child deaths each year. Despite healthy levels of economic growth, many of South Asia's countries have persistent and unacceptable levels of malnutrition with complex causality. South Asia has both the highest rates and the largest numbers of malnutrition in the world. Gender inequality and social exclusion are at the heart of the malnutrition problem in South Asia. About 23% (336 million) of the population in South Asia are routinely hungry, without access to enough calories, every day. This is greatly undermining human development and limiting South Asia's productivity with potential GDP loss estimates up to 3%. The funding of this initiative for SAFANSI will be a grant payment to a multi-donor trust fund administered by the World Bank, who will oversee activities to advance MDGs 1c, 4 and 5. The total value of this multi-country initiative is $5.77 million over 3 years, starting 2010-11.

title: 61-13104012-KAT (Education) Promoting education for sustainable development with a particular focus on integrating disaster risk reduction and management in the education sector
description:
Initial meetings and consultations were held with Nepal National Commission for UNESCO, teacher training centres, curriculum development centres and other key stakeholder in order to prepare modalities to build the capacity of education officials on DRR and its integration in education sector.
• Participating regularly in Education Cluster Group Meeting on emergency on disaster risk reduction and emergency support response
• A 2 days' workshop was jointly organized by MOE, UNICEF, SC and UNESCO with the support of UNESCO Bangkok Office on DRR in education sector with a view to reach agreement on a coherent and holistic approach to DRR in the education sector and to explore strategic options for integrating DRR into education sectorial planning, and how partners can support this. 70 participants from MOE, UN agencies, development partners and I/NGOs participated in the workshop. Workshop was facilitated by UNESCO, UNICEF and Nepal Risk reduction consortium's expert

• With the support of NRC secondee a mapping of DRR activities in Nepal's Education Sector has been undertaken and shared during the 2 days joint workshop on DRR in education sector held in January 2012.
• A flyer on "DRR in Education an imperative for education policymakers" prepared by UNESCO Bangkok has been chosen by education cluster group for its adaption and translation into Nepali language as an advocacy materials.

• Meetings with key stakeholders have contributed to enhance understanding on the importance of DRR in education and bring all key stakeholders on board and work together to build the capacity of education officials on DRR in education including integration of DRR into teacher training and curriculum.

• A 2 days' workshop contributed to enhance understating on DRR in education among education officials and other key stakeholders. The workshop agreed on 10 key actions to be undertaken in next 12 months as road map for DRR in education. • Analysis of mapping and other materials shared during the workshop further contributed in raising the awareness among participants on DRR in education.

• Integrating DRR in education demand huge capacity including conceptual clarity among key stakeholder

• Collaboration with Nepal National commission for UNESCO, MOE, UN agencies contributes brings key stakeholders to work together and also ensures cost effectiveness and sustainability of teh programme.

title: Jaladh Integrated Watershed and Natural Resource Management Program
description:
• The concept of Open Village School will be established under which 2600 villagers will receive training on eco-literacy, bio-intensive gardening, watershed literacy, livestock management, local history and geography, current affairs, natural pest management, primary health, women’s rights, gender based violence and other topics.
  • 525 people will get orientation on HIV/AIDS, sexual and reproductive health rights, natural resource management, democracy and other topics.
  • 14 different training packages for illiterate people will be developed and distributed.
  • 225 people within the villages will receive training/ develop skills in facilitation, teaching and organisation.
  • 1,650 people will attend meetings and discussions.
  • Capacity building and infrastructure development will be provided to Jaladh Youth Club. Under the initiative, 950 school youth will receive training/ orientation in ecology, watersheds, history, the global challenges, agro-ecology, family planning, HIV/AIDS and sexual and reproductive health rights.
  • 18 learning resource centres with audio-visual capacities will be established and managed
  • 80 youth (both boys and girls) will receive training and develop skills in facilitation and organisation
  • 470 (other) girls and boys will participate in meetings, village activities, advocacy and campaign work.
  • About 2699 people will receive Functional Literacy
  • Approximately three community based organisations and 10 village organisations will be established.
  • Apart from other regular study tours, information and documentation activities,  the project will establish a 400 m2 of demonstration garden at the Life school center
  • Under Rural Workers and Crafts People’s Programme (RWCPP) 200 landless will receive training on new technical skills and efforts will be catered towards providing and use rights to 200 others.
  • 144 landless people will receive training/ basic skills in conducting meetings, basic primary health care, trade unions and other issues.
  • Participatory Conservation and Community Activities Programme (PCCAP) of the project will assist  in preparing 100 village plan/projects
  • Group Partnership Programme (GPP)  will help form and operationalise 18 cooperatives with lead representation from poor and socially excluded families
  • 35 groups will receive training/ skills to improved their natural resource management capacity
  • The Whole Watershed Programme (WWP) hopes to ensure access of  100 households to natural resources. This also hopes to conserve and manage 200ha of currently fragile land.
  • Advocacy and Policy Dialogue Programme (APD) will provide training/orientation on basic advocacy skills to 500 men and women. Similarly, Advocacy campaign will be conducted for popular co-management  of Churia

title: Enhancing Mobile Population Access to HIV/AIDs Service, Information & Support (EMPHASIS)
description:
1. Prevention services through establishing linkages with the existing government services in the source, transit and destination locations.
  2. Treatment, care and support through establishing linkages with public and private service providers at source and destination points to ensure continuity of services across the continuum of mobility without interruption
  3. Reducing the vulnerability of mobile women in sex work and wives of mobile men at the source areas
  4. Establishing and strengthening community based organizations, local government and NGO’s to reduce vulnerability of mobile populations
  5. Linking NGOs and CBOs at source, transit and destination through use of appropriate information and communication technology and establishment of a database to connect between mobile populations and their families in source, transit and destination areas
  6. Sensitizing and orienting people with whom mobile populations will come into contact such as transport organizations, highway hoteliers, traders, border security personnel,  customs and other local officials at transit points; improving their ability and effectiveness in advising mobile populations, with a particular focus on the specific vulnerabilities and denial of rights faced by mobile women.
  7. A regional research centre - the project envisages the establishment of a regional research centre on HIV and mobility, managed by The Overseas Development Institute (ODI), which will house all the information and data about mobility and HIV in the region and undertake specific research, surveys and studies on a regular basis to ensure availability and quality of information to support the efforts of evidence based advocacy at national and regional levels
  8. Research studies - will be conducted to better understand the gender dynamics and gender based vulnerabilities of mobile populations and their family members
  9. Monitoring and Evaluation - The project management unit will work with the research centre to monitor and evaluate the project, in order to guarantee that the learning cycle is active and constantly feeds into more effective implementation, resulting in better practice

title: COUNTRY PROGRAMME ACTION PLAN (CPAP), 2008-2010 (extended to 2012) for the Programme of Cooperation between The Government of Nepal and The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)
description:
Reproductive Health

  • Advocacy with politicians, policy makers, civil society, community leaders—and emphasizing the involvement of men—to address key RH, ASRH, prolapse, gender and social-inclusion issues.
  • Strengthening the institutional capacity of Divisions under the Department of Health to deliver RH services.
  • Strengthening the technical proficiency of health-service personnel to provide client-friendly RH services including safe motherhood, family planning, ASRH and GBV.
  • Strengthen partnerships and capacity of I/NGOs for technical advisory services on BCC and communication strategies for uterine prolapse, quality of care, ASRH and FP.
  • Enhancing the institutional capacity of implementing partners at district level and below to deliver quality RH services including support the establishment of BEOC sites; (g) strengthen the referral system at district level; (h) support the revitalization of PHC ORCs at district level;
  • Enhancing the skills of service providers in providing quality RH services.
  • Support for mobile outreach services.
  • Training district/community level on RH, gender and social inclusion;
  • Establishing a supportive environment for ASRH activities. A key activity will be to orient community gatekeepers on ASRH issues.
  • Capacity building of sex workers in combating HIV-AIDS, increase women’s negotiation skills for safe sex, ensure the availability of condoms, disseminate information especially on the feminization of HIV/AIDS, and integrate HIV issues into RH services at the district level.
  • Support for “Choose Your Future” programme for girls, peer education programme;
  • Strengthening the technical proficiency health-service providers on youth- friendly ASRH services and teachers on ASRH and HIV/AIDS using student-friendly methodologies.

Population and Development

  • Support training needs assessment and train staff of statistical offices and Implementing Partners at central and district levels;
  • Equipment for census data production and dissemination to line ministries at national level and DDCs of project districts;
  • Development and implementation of a plan for the 2011 population census;
  • Development of advocacy materials for policy makers, religious leaders, uniformed forces and the general public on emerging population and development issues;
  • Develop and institutionalize an integrated data and information management system, including DPMAS for monitoring of indicators at district level;
  • Establish baseline and endline information for monitoring and evaluation of the CPAP;
  • Provide technical support for the 2011 Population and Housing Census;
  • Conduct surveys on RH, migration, SGBV and conflict-related issues to inform policy decision on IDPs, ex-combatants, refugees and persons affected by emergencies;
  • Undertake evidence-based advocacy and sensitization of policy and decision makers and civil society on emerging PD issues such as migration, urbanisation, youth, aging, sex ratio at birth;
  • Building capacities of partner institutions to integrate population, gender, RH, social inclusion, peace-building and emergency concerns into their plans and programmes;
  • Integration of the Nepal Population Perspective Plan into the Government’s development plans;
  • Training to national and district level staff on programme management, M&E evaluation and integration of population concerns into development plans and programmes.

Gender 

  • Support to (a) the GoN’s programmes for reintegration of ex-combatants and internally displaced women, and implementation of UN Resolution 1325;
  • Mainstream SGBV in training modules of health sector;
  • Enhance capacity in community-based monitoring initiatives with health facilities for tracking SGBV;
  • Conduct evidence-based capacity-building of police, lawyers and media on caste and GBV;
  • Increasing public awareness about role of males in violence prevention;
  • Strengthening local capacity to monitor and respond to SGBV together with other actors;
  • Building capacity of women, especially of excluded groups, to participate in design and implementation of peace-building initiatives;
  • Develop and implement a National Action Plan on UNSCR 1325; (b) develop directives and action plan on reintegration of women affected by conflict; and (c) support analytical evidence-base submissions to the CA on gender and women’s protection and reintegration issues;
  • Support access to justice and rehabilitation for women affected by GBV during conflict in selected districts;
  • Develop a national action plan on UNSCR 1325;
  • Mainstreaming gender in planning and monitoring mechanisms in the health sector and in the police will be supported;
  • Strengthen gender-responsive mechanisms in the police and justice sectors; (d) develop a database for evidence-based advocacy on GBV;
  • Strengthen community-based gender- and social-inclusion monitoring systems;
  • Conduct evidence-based advocacy for integration of GBV in planning and M&E mechanisms of select institutions.

title: Policy assistance for bio-secure agro-food supply chain enhanced market access and food security for the small holding rural sector
description:
1.1. Recruitment of national and TCDC consultants

1.2. Conduct National stakeholders’ workshop / meetings

1.3 Review the current situation of level of bio-security in the agro-food supply chain and identify policy and institutional constraints to transform the agro-food supply chain into bio-secure

1.4 Develop a draft on national policy framework and institutional reform        necessary  for  bio-security based on the analysis of economic benefits

1.5. Draft a national food safety and quality policy (to fit within the national policy framework) and develop the action plan for implementation of the same

1.6. Analyze and prepare risk analysis and management frameworks

2.1. Assess the existing situation on the role of public and private sectors on agro-food supply chain and of level of bio-security in the agro-food supply chain covering role of various stakeholders including farmers, producers, processors, transporters, other service providers, retailers, consumers, etc

2.2. Review the cost of compliance with bio-secure requirements (Prepare/design an analytical framework and assist in its implementation in a selected area, in collaboration with the National Consultants, to estimate the cost of adopting bio-secure practices (i.e GAP) by small farmers)

3.1. Conduct a National stakeholders’ workshop / meetings and develop training modules for ToT and subject specific trainings, and their curricula and materials

3.2. Organize a ToT (12- 15 days) and develop Master Trainers (15-20 Participants)

3.3. Carry out various level in-country trainings to the participants of the   public and private sectors on the subject of bio-secure agriculture

3.4. Carry out on the job training for the operation and troubleshooting of HPLC and LCMS to analyze contaminants, residues, additives, etc. in food and feeds in abroad country

3.5. In-country/onsite training on LCMS, GCMS for operation and troubleshooting   on  analysis of contaminants, residues, additives, etc. in food and feed materials by TCDC experts

4.1. Develop standards of the NTIS identified exportable commodities including coffee and dairy products that are in harmony with Codex

4.2. Strengthen laboratory-testing facility for the analysis of contaminants especially heavy metals, pesticides and veterinary drug residues.

4.3. Operationalize CODEX national secretariat for continual standard development as well as establishment and strengthening of National Codex Committees

description:
A description of the main activities of the project 

3.1  Coordination, advocacy and monitoring of the implementation of the National Plan of Action for Children with regard to child protection by a national multi-sector multi-institution child protection mechanism.

3.2  Coordination of interventions and referral mechanisms, mobilisation of resources and monitoring with regard to child protection by District Child Welfare Boards/DCPC/VCPC in 23 Child-Friendly Local Governance (CFLG) districts.

3.3  Incorporation of child protection in the plans & budgets and social mobilisation activities of district, village, ward and community structures under LGCDP in 23 Child Friendly Local Governance (CFLG) districts.

3.4  Incorporation of child protection in education and health systems in selected districts.

Dissemination of information/promotion of behaviour change with all children & families, detection and referral of children at risk and children in harmful situations, case monitoring, reporting & follow-up by Paralegal Committees(PLC´s) in 75 districts.

A description of the main activities of the project

title: Koshi Basin Program Phase 1 (ICIMOD)
description: The Intergovernmental Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) initiative provides funding for a 'multi-disciplinary river basin resource management programme' targeting the Koshi River Basin, covering parts of China, Nepal, and India.  The overall goal is to contribute to inclusive poverty reduction and enhanced resilience to climate change by securing and sustaining freshwater ecosystem services. Australia's contribution will: develop a basin wide knowledge based in a web-based information sharing platform; propose options for improved agriculture in different geo-climatic parts of the basin; and provide detailed case studies of the underlying causes and management options for a range of water hazards. Improving the management of the waters of the Himalayan Rivers is critical to improving the livelihood of more than 500 million of the world's poorest people. The total value of this multi-country initiative is $3.0 million over 4 years, starting 2011-12.

title: Trial Bridge Sub Sector Programme III
description:
Districts are the main implementers at the operational level. It supports the local communities in building their own bridges. As the beneficiaries themselves can best assess the need for a bridge, the communities initiate the bridge demand along with their commitment to mobilise local resources (labour and local materials), plus their willingness to assume responsibilities, prove the feasibility of the venture, and finally they construct a bridge. In this context, a comprehensive bridge demand of over 6000 bridges across the country has been compiled. Every year, according to the budget availability, these are screened and prioritised through a set of criteria such as distance gained, population served (giving higher weightage to DAGs), accidents occurred due to the absence of the bridge. The UC then takes the lead role for the completion of a bridge. For this purpose, an Agreement is established between the concerned UC and the DDC. Transparency is maintained at all stages through various tools like: public hearing/auditing, fact sheets, third party technical audit and participatory decision making process. Only local people are given the opportunity to work on the construction and the maintenance work of trail bridges. Another important aspect is the monitoring to ensure that equal wages are paid for equal work. Efforts are made to ensure that labourers are insured against death and accidents. Formation of an inclusive UC is one of the major tasks to ensure conflict sensitivity. The representation of women in the UCs is aimed at 33% with executive posts provisioned for DAGs in order to help address the needs of the DAG members.

 

Trail Bridge SWAp Coordination Committee ("TBSCC") is established as an apex level body comprising representatives of GoN as well as that of all development partners supporting TB SWAp, to give direction/guidance to the implementation of the TB SWAp. DoLIDAR is the executing agency on behalf of GoN and Trail Bridge Support Unit (TBSU)/Helvetas is the TA provider on behalf of SDC. SDC proposes to continue with Helvetas for this final phase (without going into a tendering process), because of their legacy and leading expertise in this field. Infact, SDC would not foresee a next phase without the involvement of Helvetas.

title: Saving Mothers’ and Infants’ Lives (SMILE)
description:
• Extensive community mobilization work will be carried out into 7 poorest performing birthing centers of the Rupandehi district where the rate of Institutional delivery is 7% (Karmahawa health Post/Birthing Center. The average % of Institutional delivery in these 7 VDCs is 19 %  (918 mother delivering into these BC out of 4914 expected pregnancies DPHO 068/69). The Birthing Centers planned to  be supported are; Ferana SHP ( Birthing Centre), Karmahawa HP (Birthing Centre), Sickthan SHP, Kerwani SHP (Birthing Centre), Devdaha SHP (Birthing Centre), Semarabazar- -Illaka HP(Birthing Centre), Basantapur PHC -Illaka (Birthing Centre) .
  • In Navalparasi, all VDCs will be covered with various MNH related activities particularly focusing on community based/women empowerment, HFOMC strengthening. However, the extensive community mobilization activities will be carried out in 17 VDCs which are selected  jointly with DHO  on the basis of remoteness and DAG mapping by DDC Nawalparasi. Out of 17 VDCs 7 are on lowest category ie IV category and 5 VDCs on III B and 7 VDCs on III A category. (Selected VDCs are; Ratanpur, Gaidakot, Rajahar, Mukundapur, Rakachuli, Dhurkot, Benimanipur, Dumkibas HP, Arkhala, Dadhajheri, Kotthar, Bulingtar PHC, Devchuli, Divaypuri, Germi, Sanai, and Palhi PHC)
  • Activate FCHVs and mothers’ groups to organize monthly meetings to analyze and address the causes of maternal death and overall position of women in society; track pregnancies and support expectant mothers to receive antenatal care, including distributing iron and folic acid supplements;
  • Mobilize mothers’ groups and FCHVs to foster behavior change by increasing the participation of decision-makers, such as mother-in-laws and men in the areas of pregnancy care and birth preparedness (i.e., identifying danger signs, place of delivery and emergency actions needed in case of complications);
  • Work with local radio and folk media to disseminate health education and behavior change messages on maternal health;
  • Engage mother-in-laws, men and youth clubs to educate them on their role to make all deliveries safe;
  • Conduct a study to identify social norms that restrict women from accessing reproductive rights, specifically maternal health services; and
  • Strengthen FCHV capacity and leadership roles, and advocate for local resources for community-based health services.
  • Renovate and provide essential equipment and supplies to 24 birthing centers in both districts where the commitment from VDCs and HFOMCs is higher to upgrade and strengthen birthing centers at the sub health post and health post levels;
  • Provide training/refresher courses on birth preparedness to 1,500 FCHVs and 550 health workers;
  • Establish and/or improve referral systems between communities, local health facilities and district service providers;
  • Provide technical support to the CBNCP and IMCI follow up and strengthening
  • Train 15 health providers to conduct normal and complicated birth deliveries (per the government’s mandate on skilled birth attendants); and
  • Organize/facilitate linkages between communities and health care providers, especially in areas where health conditions are the worst. Specifically, CARE will replicate our experience working on Partnership Defined Quality, a proven tool that involves supervisor observation checklists, exit interviews and scorecards to enhance health provider performance and client satisfaction. This process will help health facilities identify their needs, explore resources to address them and upgrade their capabilities.

 

  • Sensitize all Health Facility Operation and Management Committee (HFOMC) members  in Navalparasi and selected VDCs’s HFOMC members in Rupendehi on various health issues affecting their communities, with a particular focus on maternal health and issues related to social and geographic exclusions, and supporting the VDC annual planning process to ensure local resources are allocated to increase access to quality maternal health care for women;
  • Organize annual review meetings with VDC-appointed secretaries to update them on project progress and provide feedback and support to VDC-initiated health activities;
  • Participate in annual planning and review meetings, working with the Ministry of Health and Population/District Reproductive Health Coordination Committees and District Public Health Offices/District Development Committees to develop a strategy, verifiable and attainable maternal health objectives and a training package for health workers;
  • Train 135 HFOMCs using a module developed by CARE and the Ministry of Health and Population to improve local health governance and service quality by promoting responsibility, accountability, transparency and predictability in health services; and
  • Facilitate annual review meetings with HFOMCs in the 135 health facilities to update progress and discuss constraints, review strategies, policies and program targets

title: High Value Agriculture Project (HVAP) in Hills and Mountains Areas
description:
In this High Value Agriculture Project in Hills and Mountains of Mid-western Region, funded by IFAD, SNV is responsible for implementation of Component 1 in which it will work together with the Local Capacity Builder Agro-Enterprise Center (AEC).

  • The Component 1 covers selection of companies for contractual production, value chain analysis, selection of producers, baselines and actual signing of contracts between the agribusinesses and the producers.
  • SNV also provides advisory services to Component 2 which provides the necessary support to the intended value chain development: formation/strengthening value chain producers groups, initiatives to promote gender and social inclusion, support for high value commodity production and post-harvest activities, establishment of a grant-based value chain development fund, and support for district operations and inclusion of remote communities. SNV has a small implementation role in Component 2 to promote gender and social within the project and among project stakeholders and contracted implementers.
  • Component 3 provides for project management and linked activities including M&E and knowledge management. Next to providing advisory services to Component 3, SNV is also responsible for the implementation of its knowledge management component.

title: Building statistical capacity for quality food security and nutrition information in support of better informed policies
description:
Activity 1.1:  Inception mission to set up the country’s multisectoral taskforce for discussing and planning the activities of both FBS and NHS in line with their terms of reference.

Activity 1.2: Regional workshop (of five days on the FAO methodological framework of preparing the supply and utilization accounts (SUA) for compiling the FBS for representatives of MoA and NSO of  participating countries.

Activity 1.3: Representatives of MoA of each country will prepare the SUA for the past four years based on the available agricultural and food data and compile the yearly FBS.

Activity 1.4: National workshop among the members of the country multisectoral taskforce to identify and to assess the progress in preparation of the SUA.

Activity 2.1: Country’s NSO staff  prepare the required data files on food consumption derived from the NHS as per FAO data files instructions. 

 Activity 2.2: Country’s NSO staff, together with the support of nutritionist from Ministry of Health, prepare the Food Composition Table of nutrients conversion factors which are essential for both updating the inputs of the SUA and for deriving FSNS.

Activity 2.3: Regional workshop of five days on the FAO methodological framework of deriving food security and nutrition statistics from the NHES for representatives of NSO and MoA of participating countries.

Activity 2.4:  Country’s NSO staff draft the food security analysis based on the results derived from the NHS in the regional workshop.

Activity 2.5: Institutional structure and the capacity of concerned departments/institutions which are engaged in nutrition statistical data collection and analysis, and their inter-linkages reviewed and technical advice provided with an aim to strengthen the institutional capacity and promote inter-ministerial/departmental coordination.

Activity 3.1: A five day National Writeshop among all representatives of the different national institutions constituting the country’s multisectoral taskforce to analyse and interpret the FBS and FSNS for the write up of the Country flagship technical “Food Security and Nutrition Status” report.

Activity 3.2:  The multisectoral taskforce finalizes the Country flagship technical “Food Security and Nutrition Status” report  within one month after the writeshop with the technical backstopping assistance of the food security analysis consultant.

Activity 3.3: Check and edit of the country flagship technical “Food Security and Nutrition Status” report by Food Security Analysis consultant and FAORAP .

Activity 3.4: National Seminar for the presentation and discussion of the country flagship technical “Food Security and Nutrition Status” by the multisectoral taskforce.

Activity 3.5:  Printing of 250 copies of the country flagship technical report, “Food Security and Nutrition Status” for dissemination.

Activity 3.6: A three day Regional Workshop will be held among representatives of the participating countries coming from the NSO, MoA and the Multisectoral taskforce coordinator for presenting countries’ results, findings and recommendations.
borrower: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
source: MoF DFMIS (Ministry of Finance - Development Finance Information Management System)

title: Supporting Investments in Water Security in River Basins
description:
This is a Regional TA funded by Asian Development Bank for Indonesia, Nepal and Uzbekistan. Estimated cost of TA is US$ 2.43 million of which US$ 2.00 million will be financed by ADB on a grant basis from Japan special Fund. JWA (Japan Water Agency) will contribute US$ 0.43 million equivalent through in-kind support. It has two components:

I. Preparation for future water resources management programs that combine structuralo and non-structural investments to increase water security in three pilot basin areas and to improve exiting river basin management plans.

II. In-country  and regional capacity development activities to prepare government agencies, river basin organizations and other stakeholders for these future investment programs, including demonstrating activities to start implementating innovative approaches to increase water securitiy in the three basins.

In the case of Nepal, the TA will help to identify investment needs in preparation for future feasibility studies for projects to increase water security in the pilot river basins of Bagmati.

title: Women Empowerment for transformation in Churia Area Project (SAKCHHAM II)
description:
1. Operations and office set up, including procurement and recruitment, selection of partners and signing of agreements.
  2. Capacity building of staff and partners on UNSCR 1325&1820, CEDAW, gender and social inclusion and policies and legislation on sexual explotation and abuse.
  3. Development of M&E plan (in cooperation with CARE Österreich),  including plan and process for project review
  4. Development of exit strategy in consultation with implementing partners.
  5. Conduct base line survey on knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP)
  6. Conduct analysis of poverty, power structures and gender analysis through assessment of Underlying Causes of Poverty, community mapping and other participatory assessment tools.
  7. Strengthen women’s community based organisations and Popular Education Centres, Local Peace Committees through capacity building.
  8. Awareness generation among VDC and DDCs,  political parties and other line agency on UNSCR 1325 and 1820, women’s rights, gender and social inclusion (training, interactions, workshop, debate and distribution of resource materials etc)
  9. Mobilisation of community based organisations of women (and others) to provide critical feedback and inputs to drafts of the constitution.
  10. Strenghtening women’s networks (N-FOWRC) from district to national levels by organizing capacity building training, interactions and providing support to organize campagins, rallies and public hearing  to end impunity and to promote women’s advancement.
  11. Develop and conduct psycho-education sessions on reactions to distress, first interventions for communities.
  12. Assessment of local/ traditional psychosocial coping mechanisms in Kapilvastu and assessment of harmful traditions.
  13. Trained local volunteers will conduct various psychosocial activities (e.g. facilitating group discussion among women facing distress to provide forum for sharing, ventilation,strengthening life skills to get affirmation and for raising awareness among these women about their rights and how they can challenge oppressive practices.)
  14. Community based support by  thorough information for women in need on institutions offering mental health, social, medical or other specialized services on basis of the assessment of services. (Provision of emergency fund to support women survivors of violence to meet their costs for medical care, tranportation, food  and shelter.)
  15. Capacity building of community based psycho social care providers, traditional healers and local health workers. Organize psychosocial care worker’s capacity building activities and provide support  to initiate interventations for wellbeing through group facilitation and mobilization
  16. Support to create a loose forum of service providers (police, health service poviders, public prosecuter, administers and concerned groups such as KOSHISH group) to share information and learnings inoder to render gender responsive service to the survivors) and creating community safety nets.
  17. Support to psychosocial care workers in terms of training in stress management, emotional support regular sharing meetings, caregiver peer support, etc.
  18. Assessment of existing services available for psychosocial and mental health care, health care, legal aid and identify gaps and advocate for addressing gaps.
  19. Facilitate linkages and coordination with professional mental health care providers, psychosocial counsellors, and other referral institutions (legal aid cells) to provide specific services to women survivors of violence (at local and national levels).
  20. Conduct workshops with influential members of community (schoolteachers, religious leaders, ward members, youth and elected women members, traditional healers), on consequences of harmful traditional practices (e.g. child marriage, etc) and provide support for regular interaction to monitor the progress.
  21. Train men as trainers on masculinities, gender based violence and social inclusion. to promote critical thinking around masculinities, gender norms and GBV and accountability
  22. Organise districts level workshops for reflection on maculinities, role of men and boys to end  GBV, women empowerment  and gender equality.
  23. Sensitisation programmes among communities (men and women) for critical thinking to promote behaviour change. Organize PEC centers at community levels for for critical thinking to promote behaviour change on harmful socio-cultural practices at household and community and awareness on UNSCR 1325/1820, gender issues, women’s rights, social exclusion and caste based discrimination.
  24. Mass awareness on UNSCR 1325/1820, gender issues, women’s rights, social exclusion (including caste based) through popular media such as radio and TV, theatre and wall newspaper.
  25. Support to demystify Constitution and legal provisions ( family law, citizeship and nationality laws and laws addressing GBV) by providing information in simple Nepali and local language and organize legal literacy through PEC centers
  26. Raise awareness and knowledge of journalists and media persons on UNSCR 1325/1820 and other related international conventions, principles and commitments
  27. Support to reach out rural PVSE community, to bring out their voice as a national issue and facilitate to monitor and report whether or not there is women’s participation in the entire process of Peace Building.
  28. Advocacy to promote participation of women in state affairs and peace process. This would include leadership training for women, conducting public hearing, social audit, campaigns, meetings, workshops. 2010 will be 10th year anniversary of UNSCR 1325 and to commerorate this, specific activities such as sharing of status report on UNSCR 1325 at various levels.
  29. Advocacy at various levels to include women’s critical feedback and inputs into draft constitution. Campaigns, lobbying, meetings at local and national level for inclusion of community feedback/ inputs into draft of the constituton. Engaging men in the process of campaigns etc.
  30. Support/ facilitation of investigation of reports on GBV and domestic violence and multiple challenges women and men face in communities upon their return home from years of war
  31. Raise awarness, build skills and knowledge of local police desk, health service providers, lawyers and public prosecuters, traditional mediators on Gender, UNSCR 1325/1820  and advocate for spearheading prosecution of crime against women and girls (at local and district levels)
  32. Leadership training for social and political women leaders at district levels. While in the new district, Kapilvastu, there would be intensive training for women leaders, in the two older districts, refresher training will be provided.
  33. Mentoring/ coaching of local women leaders by established and successful women leaders through interactions, consultations, sharing meetings and resource materials.
  34. Technical and financial support to women members of political parties to influence party agenda and for PVSE women to be represented in decision making positions within party structures (include analysis of party policy, manifesto, interaction with leaders)
  35. Training of Trainers (on UNSCR 1325/1820, gender and social inclusion, and treaties related to women) training to district level trainers, Local Resource Persons and women’s rights activists to mainstream agenda at all levels.
  36. Capacity building on UNSCR 1325/ 1820, women’s rights, gender and social inclusion for community based organisations, networks., coalitions, local government,  and other stakeholders (trainings, orientation, workshop and interactions).This activity will be more intensive in new district, Kapilvastu.
  37. Capacity building of local level Peace (LPC) Committees on UNSCR 1325/1820 and state acountability .
  38. Identification and capacity building of local resource persons on initiating and managing IGP with women
  39. Capacity building of women on entrepreneurship, cooperative management, savings and credit and specific vocational skill training.
  40. Provide material support for enterprise/ income generating activity
  41. Provide support to women’s economic organisation in terms of seed money, logistics, coaching, linking and exposure visits.
  42. Capacity building (through training/ workshops and meetings) of development committees at village and district level on UCP analysis and planning for development of target group.
  43. Assessment of existing schemes and support from government and non governmental sources for promoting income generation with women.
  44. Formation of women into different types of economic organisation such as savings and credit group (VSLA), cooperatives, etc.
  45. minimum wages, saftey with employers and local labour officials land rights/ land ownership certificates.Organise women’s community based organisations to lobby for minimum wages with employers and local labour officials.
  46. Mobilise women and communities to campaign with concerned government departments for greater access to employment schemes, public resources such as water, common land, forest where women and excluded communities are denied access (campaigns, interactions)
  47. Raise awarness of men and women around migration issues and facilitate link with organizations for safe employment  opportunity
  48. Engage VDC stakeholders in the UCP analysis process; participate in planning process and influence resource allocation for Dalit and women empowerment activities. Mobilize speacial interests community groups to create pressure on the VDC and other stakeholders.
  49. Assessement of women's organisations and networks (their common issues, overlap, coverage etc); dissemination and sharing.
  50. Assessment of local/traditional psychosocial coping mechanisms (protective and risk factors)
  51. Assessment of existing services available for psychosocial and mental health care, health care, legal aid, 
  52.  
  53. Establish a resource center in Bharatpur cluster where policies laws and other related documents films etc available at the national and regional level will be placed for use of civil society and others
  54. A literature review of relevant policies as they impact target group (poor vulnerable and socially excluded women) will be undertaken.
  55. Quarterly reflection workshops will be organised at the district level for women beneficiaries, implementing partners and staff.
  56. Annual Reflection Workshops will be organised at the national level. Select women beneficiaries, implementing partners and CARE staff will participate in this.

title: Nepal Earthquake Response Project (NERP)
description:
Shelter Activities

Inputs

  1. Identification of earthquake affected families/ households in coordination with government authority and key stakeholders of the targeted communities.

  3. Preparation of the list of earthquake affected families/households for cash distribution.

  5. Awareness building on gender and protection while constructing temporary and intermediate shelter.

Water Activities

1.1-14 Availability of the adequate budget for the proposed activities.

Sanitation Activities

Inputs

2.1    Needs assessment of the damaged of household and developing action plan.

3.2    Construction of permanent school new latrines.

title: Towards Achieving the Elimination of the Worst Forms of Child Labour as Priority (ACHIEVE)
description:
- Review the report and data of the 2010 Child Labour Survey and prepare estimates to identify areas of high concentration of hazardous child labour at the district level.

- Prepare a District Mainstreaming Strategy in a from of a briefing note and identify key entry points in the various plans and frameworks (including those related to the economic and social empowerment of the families).

- Identify most feasible monitoring and reporting mechanisms to integrate child labour issue, particularly those linked with district/national planning mechanisms.

-  Prepare a simple and low-cost ‘how-to’ manual (including tools and estimations) to serve as guidance for replication/adaptation of the model by other districts/sub-districts.

- Identify the most appropriate survey for purposes of identifying the number of children in the worst forms of child labour, age-group, gender, socio-economic status of the family, education status, workplaces where children are working including mapping of services and service providers  for referrals and mainstreaming purpose. 

- Develop social mobilization strategy to bring community members (including community leaders, families, school teachers, hospitals, youth, human rights groups and children among others) on-board.

- Through involvement of social partners, seek participation of employers and workers and their groups in programs, campaigns and referral processes in the two districts to ensure that children of legal working age are protected and those below working age are not involved in the worst forms or hazardous forms of child labour.

- Identify and facilitate linkages through joint programmes with schools, training and other services in cooperation with the DWCB and Child Protection/Welfare Committees

- Organize ToT for 50 national trainers using the Capacity Development Training Module prepared under Child Labour Phase I Project in cooperation with the MoLE/CLERS.

-  Reach out to 200 individuals and relevant stakeholders from various agencies to mainstream child labour elements in their programs and curricula based on the Manuals and Guidelines developed by the Project.

- In collaboration with the CLERS, social partners, prepare a campaign module on workplace corporal punishment, Occupational Safety and Health and other workplace issues related to child labour and children at legal working age to contribute to the efforts of the SAIEVAC campaign in Nepal which can be replicated in other countries.

- Review national laws on child labour and those related to child labour.

title: Nepal Earthquake Response Programme- Disaster Risk Reduction in recovery and reconstruction for most affected population in Nepal
description:
• Form Local Disaster Management Committees (LDMC) at VDC level and train them on the inclusive and flexible local Disaster Risk Management Planning (LDRMP) process
  • Carry out LDRMP process at VDC level and produce the LDRMP
  • Train VDC board on mainstreaming DRR in their local planning process, linking LDRMP to VDC annual development plan
  • Support Citizen Awareness Center (CAC) to facilitate community dialogue on DRR, empowerment, and governance and document evidence and lessons learned
  • Train CSOs on DRR mainstreaming and advocacy for enhancing accountability of local authorities and service providers on DRR and support to participate in VDC regular planning and reconstruction process
  • Support LDMC to implement small scale mitigation measures identified in LDRMP
  • Support CSOs to organize multi-stakeholders dialogue at VDC level on DRR and reconstruction process
  • Organize workshops and trainings at district level to orient on inclusive DRR and resilience approaches
  • Facilitate and support DDRCs to develop tools and SOPs for coordination and information management for effective disaster response and implement SOP
  • Provide training to members of the sectoral planning committees of DDC to mainstream DRR into district development planning process
  • Build capacity of district level government agencies to monitor the implementation of inclusive LDRMP, DDP, and DPRP aligned with the local self-governance act (LSGA 1999) and minimum conditions performance measures (MCPM)
  • Support DDRC to review and update the inclusive district preparedness and response plan (DPRPs) based on Vulnerability and Capacity Assessments (VCAs) from the VDCs.
  • Workshop to review inclusive and flexible LDRMP model to agree on the process and key contents to roll out in the district and VDC level
  • Conduct a study in stock taking the status of DRR mainstreaming in local development and recovery and reconstruction process and share its findings to concerned stakeholders Facilitate lobbying and interaction with CA members, parliament committees, senior government officials and political leaders in collaboration with media, civil society and peer organizations for the endorsement of the DRR policy/action plan based on Sendai framework for DRR
  • Support concerned ministries (MOHA, NPC & MoFALD) to review / develop national DRM Policy /guidelines
  • Provide inputs to Ministry of Federal Affairs and Local Development (MOFALD) on the Local Disaster Risk Management Planning (LDRMP) guidelines, based on learning from the four districts and the application of the inclusive and flexible LDRMP model
  • Organize district and national sharing workshops on good practices among the key DRR stakeholders
  • Train and support communities and market actors to construct and sustain “safe and accessible” toilets and develop Open Defecation Free strategies and WASH contingency plans
  • Implement  inclusive hygiene promotion campaigns to restore and improve hygiene behaviors interrupted by the earthquakes and to build resilience in communities through behavior change
  • Put in place risk-sensitive water supply systems for communities that have earthquake impacted water access and strengthen water supply system functionality by facilitating the re-forming of inclusive Water Supply Users Committees (WSUCs), building their capacity
  • Support for restocking of small livestock and repairing relevant infrastructure in 2 VDCs
  • Support most-vulnerable HHs with essential seeds, seeds storage facilities and irrigation channel repair
  • Support capacity building/skill development trainings and materials based on community needs

title: Building Resilience of Communities through Inclusive and Risk-aware Reconstruction and Development in Post-Earthquake.
description:
ASB’s proposed interventions for Dhading, Nalang VDC; implementing NGO partner – EPF Nepal:

  1. Establish and operationalize one interlocking adobe brick production facility (including training of all employees selected from the community)
  2. Train at least 144 families on multi-hazard resistant interlocking adobe brick method and safer building construction practices;
  3. Support at least 144 families whose houses were totally destroyed during the earthquake in building multi-hazard (earthquake, fire, heavy winds) resistant houses;
  4. Link one sustaining enterprise to the brick production center;
  5. Support construction of at least 144 household toilets;
  6. Organize awareness raising campaign on safe hygiene and sanitation practices, and promote GoN’s Open Defecation Free (ODF) initiative, reaching at least 2,500 beneficiaries;
  7. Establish and fully operationalize one Community Information and Support Centre (CISC), including capacity building of the CISC management committee and staff (i.e. librarian, greenhouse cultivator, etc.);
  8. Establish two sustaining enterprises (greenhouse and a public toolshed) on the premises of CISC;
  9. Provide information services and outreach programs on health, agriculture, disaster risk reduction, etc. issues to at least 2,500 individuals through the CISC;
  10. Train at least 1,000 individuals during the 60 training sessions organized by the CISC;
  11. Support at least 600 persons in adapting innovative approaches to agriculture and making use of the public toolshed.

ASB’s proposed interventions for Dolakha, Bhimeshwar municipality; implementing NGO partner – RIRC:

  1. Reconstruct and equip one Community Library adhering to the safe building construction norms and the principles/ standards for disability inclusion;
  2. Implement at least of at least 30 community-based disaster risk management (CBDRM) activities (i.e. training, drills and simulation exercises, development of DRM plan at the local level, etc.), engaging especially vulnerable/ at-risk populations (i.e. persons with disabilities, children, elderly, etc.);
  3. Develop and adapt to the needs of especially vulnerable/ at-risk groups (i.e. persons with disabilities) at least 5 different Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials;
  4. Disseminate the DRR IEC materials, including through the use of innovative ICT technologies, reaching in total at least 4,000 community members (men and women), including children, women, youth, elderly and marginalized communities (Dalits and Janajatis);
  5. Provide needs-based training on agriculture, livelihoods and women’s empowerment to at least 500 people through the Community Library.
