title: Enhancing the Ability of Women to Obtain Comprehensive Abortion Care and Prevent Unwanted Pregnancy- II
description:
• Conduct assessment/baseline of all possible sites in new districts, district level orientation meetings with DHO team/stakeholders and formation and orientation to Provider Support Team (PST).
  • Provide basic (equipment’s and infrastructures) supports  to ensure quality services (major supports includes equipment, instruments, furniture, drugs, minor repair of facilities) in new sites
  • Provide follow up/maintance support to provide quality services to all HFs (major supports includes equipment, instruments, furniture, drugs, minor repair of facilities)
  • Conduct orientation of Clinical Mentors and Public health nurses to develop their capacity to perform effective clinical support to all service providers of MA and 2nd trim services
  • Support training centers with equipment and supplies and conduct quality training for service providers
  • Conduct post training follow up visits to ensure quality of services by the experts on this area like Staff Nurses, Medical Doctors, Obstetricians and Gynecologists as per the level of service providers
  • Building skills of service providers on how deal and counsel with youths when they visit in health facility for services and youth members on how to actively participate in the meeting and disseminate message with their peers. This will help to strengthen health facility as youth friendly services.
  • Implement Client Oriented: Providers Efficient (COPE) and Partnership Define Quality for Youth (PDQY) quality improvement approach in all health facilities to improve quality of services
  • Conduct Annual review/networking meeting of service providers and PST members of MA and 2nd trim services
  • Provide skills and knowledge of Female Community Health Volunteers (FCHVs) on SAS and using Urine Pregnancy Test- Provide Bag, Umbrella, Urine Pregnancy Test kits, flipcharts, IEC/BCC etc.
  • Implement Social Behavior Change Communication activities to increase awareness and reduce abortion stigma at community level by collaborating with DHO/DPHOs and trained HF staff. They will use the Behavior Change Communication approaches like community dialogue meetings with local leaders and community members.
  • Develop capacity of national NGOs and local CSOs/CBOs on safe abortion and behavior change communications. Help national NGO to implement round table dialogue with key stakeholders on various issues and local CSOs/SBOs to implement community level activities to increase awareness and reduce stigma  on safe abortion
  • Coordination and joint advocacy meeting with local government bodies
  • Collect project related data from the intervention health facility once a month. Prepare report and use data for program improvement and submit to concerned agencies and conduct review meeting.
  • Conduct Client exit interview to assess the satisfaction level of women and girls who received safe abortion service. Prepare report and improve the quality of service based on the findings of the report
  • Conduct safe abortion related studies including dissemination of results in larger group.
  • Conduct assessment on the current status of sustainability of safe abortion program. After this report, develop action plan to improve further
  • Develop Costed National Plan for SAS together with GON relevant agencies
  • Piloting of facility graduation and conduct midterm evaluation.
  • Conduct pre-service training to Obstetrician/Gynecology Course. This will help to reduce time and cost to do further training after they pass from the University
  • Conduct advocacy meeting with central and local level stakeholders including TCIC and RHWG and other forums like annual review meeting
  • Conduct Social Audit (Yearly) to disseminate the progresses, challenges, lesson learnt, budget expenses and human resources of the organization.
  • Conduct Central Project Advisory Committee (CPAC) meetings, District Project Advisory Committee (DPAC) meetings and Reproductive Health Coordination Committee (RHCC) meetings
  • Conduct Project Dissemination Workshop at the end of the project to disseminate about the progresses, challenges and lessor learnt. Participants includes government and non-government stakeholders, media persons, representative from the district, CSO/CBOs, community and service users.

title: Safe, durable bamboo housing solutions (Phase - 2)
description:
1.1.1       Improve bamboo treatment processes to increase production (quantity/speed), improve quality, and/or reduce costs.

1.        Continuous assessment of bamboo treatment center (technical and business)

·         A Business Advisor to develop and support a business plan for 2 treatment centers (e.g. market linkages, promotions)

·         Ensure Partners take ownership of the treatment center and maintain a record-keeping of treated bamboo. Develop QA/QC document to ensure quality treated bamboo poles. NGO partners would be responsible for funding and following up on proposed treatment center changes.

·         A partial financial contribution for infrastructure upgrades relating to quality assurance can be provided if required.

2.       Promote and support bamboo farming

·         This would include identifying bamboo farms and providing bamboo harvest tips and training

·         Support linkages between farms and treatment centers. (Agreements with bamboo farmers including negotiating of prices, quantities, and timely deliveries)

3.       ·         Proposed changes/improvement plans that take into account market affordability. They will also include financial viability projections of treatment center operations.·         Provide support to all four NGOs with the expectation that at least two NGO partners will reach implementation at scale.·         NGO partners to carry out changes.Habitat Nepal seeks technical support from the Hilti foundation and its partners to commission a study proving/validating the strength and durability of treated bamboo, particularly concerning untreated bamboo.

 

1.1.2       Design bamboo housing models and construction technologies.

1.        Continued design consultation (community, local body, partner) and revisions to design as per need. Constant design review from all parties (community, local body, partner, Habitat, Base Bahay) for finalization of designs.

2.       Incorporate feedback from communities and other stakeholders into new house designs. Design a bamboo house costing less than $3,300 in direct construction costs in order to accommodate communities’ capacity and local government budgets.

3.       Designs accommodating incremental housing construction to be developed: (a) affordable bamboo designs that adjust to family size; (b) a bamboo vertical extension design for second floors. (c) extension component.

4.       BASE and Habitat to engage national research institutes during the design process to encourage local awareness and knowledge of the technology.

5.       Design consultation and review with the local bodies for a durable and disaster-resilient bamboo public building to construct in collaboration with the local government in a strategic location.

6.       Continuous communication with Base Bahay for improvement of house designs appropriate to the context.

1.1.3       construction of 500 houses through a cost-sharing grant scheme with the Government aimed at low-income families living in vulnerable conditions.

1.        Government coordination for expanding and replicating the Hilti fondation housing project model to several locations.

2.       Houses will be built for disaster-affected, marginalized ethnic groups and/or highly vulnerable families, attracting the participation of LGUs, given their mandate to address the housing needs of such population.

3.       Local government units (LGU) will provide land (where necessary), release funds allocated for housing, and grant or facilitate approvals necessary. 

4.       Habitat Nepal will offer a partial cost-sharing (with the Hilti foundation support) to ensure sufficient leadership over the project.

5.       Habitat Nepal will provide technical support for land assessment, plotting of land, drawings, and supervision on the construction site for the families.

6.       Habitat Nepal will provide social support and conduct a baseline survey to ensure target communities receive housing and that communities are motivated to work on their houses.

1.1.4      Develop Market-based Approach to encourage families to choose to build with bamboo.

1.        Applying a HCD (human-centered design) approach, rapid prototype solutions that will increase the adoption of bamboo housing solutions on the demand-side.

2.       Pilot test most promising strategies during year 2.

3.       Support to providers - including contractors, hardware stores, treatment centers, and others - from a technical and business perspective to ensure sustainable mechanisms for delivering treated bamboo solutions in the Eastern Terai.

4.       Monitor and evaluate outcomes by end of Phase II, with the intention of defining scale up strategies.

1.1.5       broader ecosystem strategy to shape perceptions and practices regarding use of treated bamboo in housing constructions.

1.        Identify and create a coalition with multi-stakeholders (government, NGOs, individuals) to jointly promote bamboo housing and influence behavior of both demand and supply-side actors.

2.       Coordinate with local government to identify possible incentive schemes to promote bamboo housing.

3.       Activities to ensure government policies accommodate treated bamboo technology in home construction

4.       Identify, design, and implement a joint promotional strategy with the Government and other stakeholders, including private sector actors.

5.       Conduct mason training to strengthen construction techniques that they can utilize for bamboo house construction.

description:
• The Program will be implemented through local NGOs. GFI Nepal will provide financial and technical support as well as monitor and evaluate the activities in accordance with the set targets.

The fund from GFI, USA will be endorsed to GFI Nepal and then it will be dispersed to partner agencies.

title: COVID-19 Emergency Response and Recovery Project (CERRP)
description:
Based on the value chain assessment, CRS COVID-19 agribusiness impact assessment study recommendations and GoN (including local municipalities) priorities, CRS Nepal will design and implement an inclusive value chain project in Palpa District. The project will not only address the short-term economic recovery needs of vulnerable households but also make their livelihood more profitable and resilient to future shocks through their integration with value chains. Based on inputs from local municipalities and feasibility assessment, the project will provide support to agribusiness SMEs to recover from the impacts of COVID-19. The support will include improved processing equipment and infrastructure (warehouse, crop storage models, drying yards, collection centers etc.) to agri-cooperatives, farmer groups and/or private enterprises with matching grants from local municipalities and/or province and district level agencies like MoLMAC, ADD and AKC. Priority will be given to functional agri-cooperatives and/or agri-business private enterprises led by women, smallholders or those situated in remote locations. In consultation with the local municipalities, a detailed criteria and process for selection of the agri-cooperatives and enterprises will be developed and implemented. Care will be taken to ensure that agri-cooperatives and enterprises, which are badly hit by the pandemic and are likely to support vulnerable households, are selected.

 

Support will also be extended to youth and returnee migrants on income generation opportunities along the various stages of value chain development for the identified commodities. Key activities will include technical training on select income generation activities such as small enterprises activities, mobile repair, plumbing, grocery start-up etc and provision of a start-up grant to encourage the trained participants to start their businesses. Those trainings will be provided to migrant returnees and vulnerable HHs by keeping 20 to 25 participants in each group based on their choice of training and these trainings will be conducted by technical staffs/consultants hired by partners and contents of those trainings will be based on the need and pre-test result of participants. Convergence with local municipalities will be explored to align with existing youth entrepreneurship development programs like the one being implemented by Tansen municipality. The trained project staff will provide necessary mentoring and troubleshooting support to the entrepreneurs in the beginning phase of their businesses.

 

Markets play a strong role directly and indirectly in the livelihoods of smallholder farmers. The project will identify agribusinesses and SMEs which are critical to the livelihoods of the targeted communities and support them with cash grants and other technical support to help them recover from the impacts of COVID-19 and facilitate market recovery in the process. Other technical support could also include linking businesses with financial institutions for larger credit support, or with suppliers for favorable transaction terms.

 

Where needed, the project will facilitate inclusion of women and other excluded groups into existing agriculture cooperatives and farmer groups to engage in commercial farming activities and increase their income to mitigate recent losses. Inclusion in these groups will also increase their access to various livelihood related government programs and subsidies. The project will provide trainings to targeted households on production and productivity enhancement for the crops/commodities identified through short-duration trainings and on-farm demonstrations where possible. Special attention will be paid to tailor the trainings (timing, duration, location, content, language, etc.) to facilitate meaningful participation from women. Following the trainings, the farmers will be provided with improved production inputs (seeds, planting material, seed treatment material, processing inputs, etc.) to encourage in adoption. These inputs will also help farmers restart their agricultural activities which might have been affected due to a shortage in availability of quality seeds and other inputs due to COVID-19 impact. The project will procure these inputs from local markets and vendors, providing support for the local economy and contributing to market recovery.

title: RESILIENT COMMUNITIES THROUGH VULNERABLE EARTHQUAKE RECOVERY (ReCoVER)
description: Improving income-generation practices and livelihood skills. Considering the profile of households—  landless, elderly, women-headed households, etc.—and likely wide geographic spread of the targeted  households, ReCoVER will focus on organizing small group trainings, field demonstrations, on-field  mentoring support and digital mediums like radio, which can address barriers like low mobility to build  the skills of target households on improved livelihood production and marketing practices.  To ensure trainings are targeted to the most common needs, and the most likely opportunities for  generating income, CRS will use the early start-up phase of the program to understand specific barriers  that selected vulnerable households face to increasing their income. Considering the COVID-19 context,  and in order to be efficient and safe, area assessments to decide the specific types of livelihood  interventions can mostly be completed remotely, in collaboration with implementing partners and key  local stakeholders like municipalities, agriculture knowledge centers, and private sector actors like local  chambers of commerce, financial service providers, cooperative groups and other value chain actors.  These stakeholders will help ReCoVER leadership tailor production and marketing interventions for the  most practical and applicable production improvements to generate income for households. CRS  technical staff will use the simple guidelines or standard operating procedures that worked in Gorkha  and Okhaldunga, and adjust them to the new working areas using the information gained in the process,  with focus on inclusion of women and vulnerable households. The customized guidance will be rolled out  across staff, partners and local agricultural extension workers to ensure uniform understanding across  program areas. CRS and partner staff will lead trainings on these guidelines through a mix of adultlearning  methodologies like classroom trainings, field visits, farmer exchange visits and practical handson  accompaniment sessions.  Due to the recent decentralization of governance in Nepal, the local municipalities are now responsible  for providing agriculture extension services to communities. The newly recruited and young extension  staff at municipalities will benefit from trainings organized by the program. ReCoVER will work with  municipality extension workers, private sector agricultural vendors and local cooperatives to ensure they  have the skills needed to support ReCoVER livelihood activities. The residual benefit of training these  local stakeholders is that the improved practices remain in the community after the program has ended.  • After building skills of targeted households on improved livelihood practices, ReCoVER will provide  improved inputs to nudge and motivate households in adopting the improved practices to increase  production. Based on experience from Gorkha and Okhaldunga, CRS anticipates that the key livelihood  sub-sectors will be market-oriented vegetable production, backyard poultry, goat rearing and postharvest  management in high value crops like large cardamom and coffee which will contribute to increase  15  in income. ReCoVER will focus on ensuring participants incorporate a few key improved marketing  practices with the aim of bringing their goods to market.

title: State Building at Local Level Phase 1
description:
3.3.1    Component 1: Capacity Building The main aim of this component is to support DDCs  to enhance the institutional and human resource capacity to deliver the basic services to people. Capacity building initiatives in this project are focused at DDC level and the main areas of capacity building may include but not be limited to: a) Strengthening financial management of DDCs b) Strengthening planning and monitoring capacity of DDC c) Strengthening capacities of DDCs on Information, reporting and documentations. This component is based on the demand of the DDCs and will be implemented in close collaboration with LGCDP.  

3.3.2 Component 2: Social Mobilization and Empowerment

Social mobilization process aims to enable communities to engage in the local level bottom up planning process in order to ensure that they access public resources. This is also a process by which the state can proactively reach to the people. This project will support the districts to institutionalize the social mobilization process in the planning and to enhance the capacity of the social mobilisers.  

3.3.3 Component 3: Financial Grant to DDCs  

The financial grant from SDC to DDCs will help to deliver services to the citizens, which have generally been too small to bring the long awaited peace dividend to the people. Revenue at the district level (taxes, fee and other service charges) is very little and hence the major source of revenue for more than 80% of the DDCs has been the grants from the central government. The proposed financial support is expected to help DDCs to ease this situation. Any support however, will be linked to improved performance and capacity building of the DDC. The increase in the district budget due to the financial grant is expected to be sustained on the long run because: i) the project will help to double their internal resource (taxes) within five years; ii) the project will help improve their performance and get a better ranking thereby qualify for extra budget from the centre; and iii) the natural increment of the grants allocated by the central government is expected to continue in the near future. These increased resources coupled with the capacity building will ensure the sustainability of the project undertakings once SDC’s support withdraws.

title: COVID - 19 Response Project in Nepal
description:
1.1.1Provide relief support (food and non-food items/materials) to target families using modality agreed with the GoN. This is a priority action given economic impact for many vulnerable families, such as those dependent on daily wage labour who cannot work during the lockdown and affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

2.1.1Support local government for health material such as PPE and other required materials/equipment .This support is primarily for district and local health facilities, District Disaster Management Committee (DDMC) and Local Disaster and Climate Resilience Committee (LDCRC).

2.1.2 Provide support to local level governments to establish or continue quarantine centers if required.

2.1.3 Support government of Nepal’s request regarding NFI (non-food items) to the most vulnerable households staying in quarantine (seasonal migrants returning from India). Additional protection assessments are also required for support.

3.1.1 Disseminate PSAs, social media, phone and video messaging on hand washing, food hygiene, personal hygiene, respiratory hygiene, maintaining personal distance and surface cleaning. (Using existing GoN materials and prescribed message, gender responsive , AGE SPECIFIC AND CHILD PROTECTION ) on COVID-19 preventive measures

3.1.2 Social Behaviour Change Communication sessions on COVID-19 hygiene practices through WASH Champions and FCHVs.

3.1.3 Work with youth groups to set up an online competition on handwashing demonstration, etc.

3.1.4 Mobilize youth networks to raise awareness on frequent and proper personal hygiene that lead to behaviour change s (using safe approaches and maintaining a required social distance).

3.1.5 Production and dissemination of education specific messages through audio using sign language  following govt and education cluster message

3.1.6 Disseminate message on radio and social media to remind parents on how they can support their young children’s:

3.1.7 Production and communication about transfer messages and IEC materials

4.1.1 Establishment of child, women and senior citizen friendly feedback mechanism  to listen the concerns, fears and questions about our work in the community.

4.1.2 Orientations on community engagement and accountability mechanism to staff of Plan and partner staff.

4.1.3 Public audit/social audit, community feedback mechanisms and Independent third party monitoring

title: Strengthening of the Quality Infrastructure for Sustainable Economic Development
description: The project is pursuing a multi-level approach to develop relevant quality infrastructure services for businesses. It provides training to the partners’ specialist and management staff in order to strengthen the capacities of organizations as a whole and enable them to be more easily integrated into international networks. The main partner is the Nepal Bureau of Standards and Metrology (NBSM). Further public partners are the Department of Food Technology and Quality Control (DFTQC) and the Department of Plant Resources (DPR). Additionally, the project cooperates with business associations from the pharmaceutical and dairy sectors. A total of three interrelated outputs are targeted: (1) Strengthening the national metrology and QI systems; (2) Improving the analytical capabilities of the Nepali food authority; (3) Quality assurance in the pharmaceutical sector and in the dairy industry. The project’s objectives are achieved through metrological and analytical lab training, qualifying auditors for specific certifications and accreditations, providing close consultation, and conducting mock audits. Furthermore, the partners are supported through the procurement of selected instruments.

title: Global Fund COVID-19 Response Mechanism (C19RM)
description:
Activities

Case management, clinical operations, and therapeutics

1.        Training for adult and pediatric ICU and ventilator care for physicians and staff in hospitals where critical care and anesthesia trained manpower is lacking.

2.       Oxygen delivery and oxygen delivery devices including non-invasive ventilators (Bi-Pap), high-flow nasal cannula HFNC and RAM cannulas for children

3.       PPE for malaria, TB and HIV programs

 

 

COVID-19 Diagnostics and testing

1.        Procurement of SARS-CoV-2 molecular assays including conventional and GeneXpert testing kits and supplies.

2.       Strengthen the quality assurance mechanisms for testing methodology, including point-of-care testing.

 

 

Infection prevention and control and protection of the health workforce

1.     Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): N-95 mask, surgical mask, face shield, disposable gloves, disposable gown, coverall PPE set, disposable shoes, hand sanitizer, sodium hypochlorite 5% solution (disinfectant).

2.    Training to health workers, community level frontline and essential staff and volunteers on COVID-19 related IPC measures, isolation and quarantine measures, and rational use of PPE.

3.    Dissemination and implementation of COVID-19 IPC guidelines for health care settings, community level providers and frontline staff

4.   Monitor and evaluate IPC guidance dissemination, implementation, and impact

5.    Infection prevention and control and protection of the health workforce

 

 

Risk communication

1.        Update national COVID-19 RCCE (Risk Communication and Community Engagement) guidelines and action plans.

2.       Identification and mapping the most marginalized and vulnerable populations of COVID-19 pandemic and HIV, TB and malaria at risk populations including women, elderly, adolescents, youth, and children, persons with disabilities, indigenous populations, refugees, migrants, and ethnic minorities, GBV survivors, PLHIV, TB survivors, LGBTIQ communities, FSW, and prisoners.

3.       Strengthening risk communication, developing specific platforms to engage with the most marginalized groups and vulnerable communities and enhance their involvement in tailoring local community engagement interventions for specific geographical regions as well as tailoring risk communication messages and interventions for gender, local language and local socio-culture context thus, improving the communities’ uptake with risk communications and interventions.

4.       Community mobilization activities that involve affected communities, key and vulnerable populations, women and girls, LGBTIQ communities, FSW or target populations (PLHIV, TB affected population) in the development of Information, Communication and Education (ICE)/BCC materials on COVID-19.

5.       Capacity building and engagement of communities in support of longer-term preparedness and emergency risk management functions.

Case management, clinical operations, and therapeutics

1.        To help with the current and any future medical surge, set up call centers for screening, triaging and dispatching ambulances and coordinate with health care facilities for acceptance and reception of patients transported by the ambulance

2.       Provide salary, training and supervision for staff supporting the above

 

 

Health products and waste management systems

Electronic Logistic Management Information System (eLMIS):

1.        Strengthening systematic and targeted scale-up of eLMIS/mSupply linking with health facilities, central and provincial stores to timely collect and distribute logistic data to attain a well-defined supply chain strategy for COVID-19 responses and HIV, TB and malaria services

2.       Comprehensive and sustainable approach for HR deployment for eLMIS interventions at the sub-national levels and Strengthening capacity building including regular stock monitoring and planning at the targeted levels and timely escalating the requirements to take actions

3.       Advocate and promote the practice of supply chain data use for both operational and strategic decision making at all levels of the in-country supply chain as well as planning for procurement

4.       Setting up of regular oversight and coordination mechanism for eLMIS

5.       Ensure the continuity of essential medicines and commodities supply

6.       Infrastructure and equipment for the collection, transport, treatment, and disposal of health care waste to ensure compliance with standards

 

 

Surveillance System and contact tracking

Health management information system (HMIS):

1.        Strengthening integrated reporting of HIV, TB and Malaria to the HMIS on District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) platform through data customization and Interoperability for data exchange

2.       Investments for HIV, TB, malaria and/or or cross-cutting/integrated data systems for routine reporting and surveillance that require more funds than originally funded in the grants due to COVID-19.

3.       Setting up supportive supervision as well as coaching and coordination mechanism in the context of COVID-19 pandemic thus, enhancing capacity development of sub-national levels and improving data quality, timeliness and completeness

4.       Case management, clinical operations, and therapeutics

5.       Field Epidemiology Training Program (FETP) to enhance the skills and knowledge of health workforce at all levels of Nepal, especially district and local levels, to investigate and respond to public health events of importance

6.       Sero-epidemiological surveillance

7.       Community surveys that monitor adherence to public health and social measures. COVID-19-induced barriers to accessing health services and socio-economic impacts

8.      Seroprevalence studies to measure vaccine effectiveness in immunized target groups

9.       Epidemiological investigation and contact tracing

 

 

Mitigation activities for HIV programs

1.        Additional lab staff in Viral load testing sites as existing staffs are involved in COVID-19 testing.

2.       Integrated HIV, TB, Malaria and COVID-19 screening and testing at Point of Entry (PoEs)

3.       COVID-19 antigen testing by existing lab staff of HIV-Migrant program

4.       Relief package including Nutrition support for PLHIV and KP communities

5.       Online psychological and other clinical consultation support and counselling for PLHIVs, KPs and staffs

6.       Strengthening e-reach for KPs and PLHIV through virtual platforms

7.       Printing and distribution of IEC/BCC materials focusing on COVID-19 

8.      Research and surveillance of COVID-19 among PLHIV/KPs

9.       Sensitization and advocacy focusing on mental health

10.   Distribution of Home isolation kits, hygiene kits and dignity kits (

11.     Access to treatment care and support for most poor returnees infected with COVID-19

12.    Weekly social media boosting and posting

13.    Insurance for district coordinators (Board member) /outreach workers

14.    Livelihood and income generation support activities

 

 

Mitigation activities for TB programs

1.       Integrated HIV, TB, Malaria and COVID-19 screening and testing at PoEs

2.      Training to dedicated Health workers on integrated screening and testing of HIV, TB, Malaria and COVID-19 at PoEs

3.      Seroprevalence survey of COVID among TB patients

4.      Community based TB case finding in hotspot areas of Local Level (LL)

5.      Strengthening TB Labs services and diagnosis through procurement of GeneXpert Machine, AC, Xpert XDR Cartridges, and power-back up

6.      Introduce Automated chest Xray reading system in seven major hospitals screening and treating high COVID-19 cases.

7.      Genomic Sequence for National TB Reference Lab (NTRL)

8.     Strengthening TB laboratories with test-kits, biosafety cabinets, and viral transport media (VTM)

9.      Infection prevention and control targeted at DR-TB Treatment centres (WASH, HCWM, IP guidelines, and PPEs) and establish follow up monitoring for adherence support of DR TB patients

10.  Oxygen Concentrators for DR referral Centres and hostels

11.    PPEs for health workers at TB and DR-TB sites; autoclaves

12.   Oximeter and ECG-digital monitor

13.   Training/Orientation to DR centres/subcentre/hostels/Outreach workers/TB focal persons – TB

14.   Printing of BCC materials

15.   Hotline services for TB, HIV and malaria

16.   Nutritional support to TB patients

 

 

Mitigation activities for Malaria programs

1.       Integrated HIV, TB, Malaria and COVID-19 screening and testing at PoEs, Dissemination of targeted messages

2.      Conduct integrated testing for malaria, TB, and HIV in symptomatic patients with history of exposure in quarantine and holding centers.

3.      Expand community management of malaria in at least 10 potential malaria risk wards

4.      Conduct IRS activity and Malaria Mobile Clinics (MMCs)

5.      Develop a costed COVID-19 mitigation plans for malaria focused on E2025

6.      Expand community Management of Malaria in 200 malaria risk wards

7.      Symptomatic Screening for malaria in 13 PoEs dissemination of targeted messages

8.     Mass LLINs distribution in high, moderate, and active foci & promote continuous distribution by mobilizing female community health volunteers (FCHVs)

9.      Development and implementation of integrated targeted messages for malaria, TB & HIV and COVID-19

10.  Resource is requested for development of integrated targeted messages for Malaria, TB & HIV and COVID-19

11.    Pilot test and roll out in all local bodies and in PoEs through FM and audio for at least 6 months.

 

 

Respond to human rights and gender related barriers to services

1.        Training on understanding and managing with increased Gender-based violence (GBV) in the COVID-19 outbreak

2.       Development, printing and distribution of IEC materials 

3.       Coordinating with entry points (HIV, TB and Malaria) to disseminate the information on GBV

4.      Addressing the need of Young Population

·         Social media content development and media boosting

·         Sensitization of Mental aspects that MHM. Group education and counselling

·         Formation of social support group, Monthly coordination meeting

·         Launch of online competitions related to Mental Health

·         Motivational Videos by Influential People. Publish op-eds

·         Virtual group meeting and support groups - RP

5.       Psychosocial support

·         Set referral mechanism with psychosocial support service providers

·         Hot-line services for referral and counselling services

·         Development of web/based smartphones platform TB applications development of software/app, testing, finalizing and also annual maintenance including cyber security of the application and data

title: Emergency Preparedness and Response Pooled Fund 2018-2021
description:
The intent of our preparedness and response work is to provide immediate life-saving assistance to disaster affected populations with a special focus on children. Save the Children provides support to affected communities ensure effective preparedness systems are in place to minimize the negative effects of disasters on children and their families. It advocates to influence and support key humanitarian actors (donors, government, I/NGOs, Nepal Red Cross Society) to prioritize children's well-being in an emergency.

The project will enhance the emergency preparedness and response capacities of Nepal country office, partners and key local authorities in an event of a mega disaster. By doing so it aims to reduce the vulnerabilities of communities severely affected by disasters through a cost-effective, efficient, timely, appropriate and coordinated humanitarian response in view of established humanitarian standards.

title: Community based Micro Health Project in Nepal
description:
Input (Project themes and subthemes):                                           

Strengthening Health Security Scheme in Nepal (Earlier called as Community-based Micro-health Insurance project in Nepal) has been implemented to strengthen the National Health Insurance Program of Nepal. The interventions are being implemented to support Health Insurance Board (HIB), basically in the areas of policy formulation as well as implementation support in selected districts. 

 

Health insurance program was launched in Nepal in the year 2016 and the program has been expanded up to 58 out of 77 districts of the country by the end of Fiscal year 2019/2020.  This shows the program has covered two-third of the total districts. However, only 8% of the population (18% of the population in program implemented districts) has been enrolled. The program aims to enroll 40% of the population by the next year.

 

The major challenge associated with national health insurance program is the disinterest of people towards health insurance program.  The recent report suggests that almost 2.2 million population were enrolled in health insurance program of which 0.5 million (almost 24% of total enrolled) did not renew their policy. With this trend, it is quiet challenging to achieve the targets of enrolling two-third of the population by 2025 and 100% enrollment by 2030.

 

MISEREOR has been funding the implementation social health security in Nepal since 2010. During the first phase (October 2010- December 2013), pilot project of CBMHI was implemented in two districts (Banke and Dhading) together with a team of Save the Children (SC), Micro Security Academy (MIA), NIRDHAN and DEPROSC Nepal. The project was conceptually new in Nepal and envisioned that the health security schemes helped reduce unforeseeable or unaffordable health care costs through calculable and regularly paid premiums among 45,000 marginal populations in two districts. The second phase (January 2014 to March 2017) of the project was the continuation of the first phase.         

 

Based on the learning of the first and second phase of community based micro health insurance program in Nepal, some issues have been identified, which were proposed for third phase (April 2017 to September 2020) of the program, the issues were:

1.          Community scheme should have government registration to get legal standing

2.          Provide complete handover of the scheme to the community and local government bodies

3.          Continue working together with government on national health security scheme and extend the coverage.

title: Evidence for Development (E4D)
description:
Component 1: Strengthening capacity of the National Statistical System (NSS) in Nepal;

£5m to support capacity development of the national statistical system in Nepal (including the Central Bureau of Statistics and other statistics-producing line ministries).  This will ensure early implementation of the forthcoming National Strategy for the Development of Statistics (NSDS).

Component 2: Strengthening GoN capacity for evidence generation and uptake;

£3m to strengthen the generation and use of evidence by key GoN policy and decision-makers, including dedicated support to the National Planning Commission (NPC).

 

Component 3: Strengthened District-level data systems and information for effective needs assessment;

Up to £5m to strengthen district-level systems and information, both nationally and with a specific focus on the Districts affected by the 2015 earthquake.  While this may include support to existing GoN district data systems (for example, DPMAS or WBRS) it will be the primary component through which DFID Nepal will support evidence generation within the Districts most-affected by the 2015 earthquake.  This programme document is intentionally flexible around earthquake response initiatives, which will ensure an opportunistic mechanism is in place to respond to emerging evidence needs.

Component 4: GoN and general Open Data Initiatives.

£2m to strengthen GoN’s aid effectiveness agenda, primarily through improving the quality and effectiveness of Open Data including the Ministry of Finance Aid Management Platform (AMP).  There are also a number of open data initiatives in Nepal outside of government and we will seek to strengthen these further.

title: Promotion of climate-resilient adaptation measures for sustainable livelihood in agroecological zones of Raptisonari Municipality, Banke district, Nepal.
description:
1.1          Formation/reformation of CDMCs at highly vulnerable settlements and facilitating the regular (bi/monthly) meetings of CDMCs by Social Mobilizers/Staff

1.2          Conduct community-level HVCA, review HVCA, household-level contingency plan, and community-level DMP development through the training of the leaders of CDMCs.

1.3          Organize training on Inclusive Community Based Disaster and Climate Resilience (ICBDCR) for DMC members

1.4          Organize task-specific skills training on climatic/ multi-hazards (flood, earthquake, fire, snakebite, etc.) for the task forces. (1) light search and rescue and first aid, (2) need assessment (IRA, MIRA, Sphere/CHS, (3) EWS,

1.5          Facilitate mock drills/simulations at community, and wards levels

1.6          Develop and disseminate IEC materials (brochure, calendar, Pana flex, hoarding board, etc.) on multi-hazards and climate risk reduction

1.7          Conduct awareness-raising sessions and campaigns on DRR-CCA (Street drama, radio jingles, door-to-door campaigns, use of social media, day celebration, etc.) involving trained DMC/task force members where applicable or relevant

1.8          Strengthen the existing EWS and disseminate the information up to the community level

1.9          Organize monsoon preparedness and EWS workshop at ward and Municipal levels and support the provisioning of life-saving equipment at vulnerable locations (CDMC/WDMC) based on assessment.

 

2.1          Develop beneficiary selection and prioritization criteria in consultation with local stakeholders and select beneficiaries based on well-being ranking

2.2          Conduct interactions with selected beneficiaries to identify their interested areas of small businesses and orient them on business plan development by organizing them in groups.

2.3          Organize off-farm training for those beneficiaries who are interested to involve in on-farm business/services. (Mobile repair, motorcycle repair, electricians, and plumbers in collaboration with CTEVT and DCSI)

2.4          Formation of farmer's groups and running farmers' field schools (FFS) classes at the community level and promote river bed farming, organic farming, intercropping, agroforestry, integrated pest management, etc. through farmers' field schools

2.5          Train community members on improved livestock management and on-farm training (crop management, off-season vegetables farming, nursery management) in coordination with RM, ward office, Cooperatives, and private sector

2.6          Provide input support to the selected social structures based on their business plan (with emphasis on incentivizing group-based interventions) for micro and small enterprises, for local value addition of agri- or cattle products

2.7          Provide agriculture and livestock input support to marginalized HHs (Such as climate resilient seeds, livestock (such as goats, and pigs), fishery, fish ponds, plastics for tunnel farming, pump sets/generators for irrigation, etc.)

2.8          Organize livestock health camps and pest management camps (as required) in collaboration with the local government

2.9          Promote flood-tolerant and drought-tolerant crop varieties (paddy, wheat, maize, etc.) through selected farmers

2.10        Collaborate with cooperatives (with the mandate of saving and credit program) for access to finance of beneficiaries, emergency funds mobilization, promotion insurance program for pet animals, crops, and individual beneficiaries, and market linkage for the production of beneficiaries

 

3.1          Conduct a scientific assessment of drought risk in coordination with local government and share findings with the community and stakeholders to inform CCA plans

3.2          Support vulnerable communities to establish small-scale mitigation/adaptation measures (like bioengineering, spurs, dyke, embankment, retaining walls, evacuation routes, culverts, etc.,) and formulate a maintenance plan for each measure

3.3          Support CFUGs to implement high-value plants plantation based on their business plan (fodder/fruit species, moringa, etc.) in degraded lands, trenching for fire risk management, construction of multi-purpose recharge ponds for fire and drought risk management, and drinking water for cattle/fishery, etc.

3.4          Support selected HHs with Biogas/electric cooking stoves to reduce fuel wood consumption and a climate-friendly environment

3.5          Organize orientation for the mason and technician regarding flood-resilient tube well, and toilets construction in the communities

3.6          Organize flood and earthquake resistance shelter construction training for the existing masons of the project location and construct a model multi-purpose emergency shelter in flood-vulnerable areas

3.7          Organize advocacy training and provide support to community groups (social structures) to prepare advocacy action plans and follow up and support to implement advocacy action plans

3.8          Follow up and support marginalized groups to implement advocacy action plans for DRR-CCA and livelihood issues

3.9          Support marginalized groups to participate in the local annual development planning process and raise DRR-CCA and livelihood issues

3.10        Involve private sector actors and government service providers (agro vets, insurance agents, input suppliers, traders, financial service providers, forest offices, etc.) in sensitizing/training farmers' groups

 

4.1          Capacity needs assessment of partners

4.2          Mobilization of Emergency Response Team (ERT)

4.3          Humanitarian logistics and supply chain management training

4.4          Develop IEC materials (posters and manual)

4.5          Coordination and networking with likeminded organizations/networks

title: Prevent Gender based Violence and Access to Gender Responsive Justice for Sundar Shanta Nepal
description:
1.1       Provide hardware Support in collaboration with local government and relevant GBV service providing CSOs/service providers to design and implement issue and need based programming to prevent gender-based violence and promote access to justice services. (The hardware support will be determined in later phase based on need such as GBV services including legal aid require to those come in Judicial Committee)

1.2       Support local led GBV network, CSO and local government stakeholder at province and municipalities level to understand needs and priorities of communities and jointly address GBV.

1.3       Capacity building training for women groups and community members in promoting community collaborations to address GBV.

1.4       In coordination with local government, GBV network, provide immediate support to the GBV victims such as health check-up and treatment, psychosocial support and livelihood support.

2.1 Develop need based, beneficiary led interactive training curricula on roles and responsibilities of Justice and security service providers (JSPs) (Judicial committee, GBV network members) under the new federal system on positive social norms.

2.2 Provide hardware support to JSPs and community to make their service accessible to community people, especially women and marginalized communities.

2.3.Collaborate with Ministry of Women, Children and Senior Citizen, Ministry for Social Development at province, National Human Rights Commission, National Women Commission and local municipalities to design joint pilot program to enhance access to justice services for women and marginalized people and prevent GBV.

2.4 In close collaboration with Province Social Development Ministry, local government stakeholders, GBV networks, JSPs and community people, IEC materials will be developed to provide information on available JSP services and change harmful social norms for more integrated response to GBV. The project will collaborate with relevant ministries to use already developed materials.

2.5 Strengthen referral pathways between JSPs, including one stop crisis management centers, judicial committee, women and children service center and shelter homes.

3.1Support exiting loose networks comprising women community leaders, CSO members and rights defenders at local level to strengthen mutual accountability and improve services.

3.2 Engage with elected/political representatives (women, Dalit and marginalized) and JSPs at provincial level and municipal level in collaborative dialogues.

3.3 Support capacity of media resulting in interactive media programming (radio and TV) and awareness outreach programmes at local and provincial level.

4.1       Development of evidence based knowledge resources on  social norms change and gender responsive justice services etc. for local and provincial CSO members, community people and other relevant stakeholders.

4.2       Provide fellowships to trained local youth researchers and journalists to produce news reports and conduct research on GVB and local governance challenges with mentoring and guidance support.

4.3       Documentation of the stories of women and marginalized voices for responsive justice services and socio-economic development issues

title: Post Earthquake Reconstruction Programme in Nepal - Building Back Better
description:
• The 6 year post-earthquake reconstruction programme started in May 2016 at the completion of DFID's humanitarian operations in country.
  • The project in its initial year has provided an array of support to meet immediate priorities of both the GoN's National Reconstruction Authority and vulnerable populations residing in some of the most affected earthquake areas. For example DFID is supporting the Housing Recovery and Reconstruction Platform (HRRP) for coordination and information management of the housing reconstruction sector; activated water and trail related programming in Gorkha, Rasuwa, Dhading and Nuwakot (DFID's focal districts); providing technical assistance to the NRA; supporting a programme on durable solutions for those displaced by the earthquake; contributed resources to the GoN's housing reconstruction cash grant programme for families whose houses have been completely or majorly damaged; enrolling of individuals to the GoN's housing grant programme in 11 most affected districts; geo-hazard assessments of over 500 vulnerable sites; housing damage survey in additional 17 moderately affected districts amongst others.
  • DFID Reconstruction Prgramme team is based in Kathmandu (headead by the Reconstruction Team Leader, Senior Reconstruction Advisor, Programme Manager and a Programme Officer); DFID also has Field Officers based in Gorkha,Dhading, Rasuwa and Nuwakot who are the main district focal points and lead on monitoring activities of DFID's work in the districts

title: Sustainable Tourism for Livelihood Recovery Project (STLRP)
description: The Sustainable Tourism for Livelihood Recovery Project (STLRP) – a joint project of the Nepal Tourism Board (NTB) and UNDP aims to contribute to the revival of the tourism sector by supporting livelihoods recovery of the most affected workers by providing short-term employment as well as enhancing the capacity of the NTB and other relevant stakeholders to accelerate recovery efforts including supporting the formulation of the National Tourism Recovery Strategy after COVID-19. The project will also initiate activities to support the long-term revival of the tourism sector by creating sustainable jobs and livelihood opportunities in partnership with the private sector; developing human resource capacity; supporting the creation of tourism-based enterprises; strengthening sector-related data and information management and digitalization, and articulating a comprehensive tourism recovery strategy. Aligned with sustainable tourism concepts, project activities will be oriented towards promoting a green economy.

title: LEAVING NO ONE BEHIND IN NEPAL’S GREEN, RESILIENT, AND INCLUSIVE RECOVERY
description: UNDP rolled out a socioeconomic recovery initiative after the COVID pandemic in 2020 in partnership with over dozen local governments. By 2022, the initiative was extended to over twenty-nine local governments. UNDP supported livelihood projects have been implemented in fifteen districts and twenty-nine local government. Over 150,000 people, out of which 51% are women, have directly benefited from these projects. These projects have been instrumental in increasing agricultural production by providing farmers with seeds, tools, equipment, technologies, and skills.

title: Prayash: Temporary Basic Income for Marginalized and Excluded Women in Nepal
description: The purpose of the Initiation Plan Document is for the UNDP efforts in response to the COVID-19 and to  quickly get off the ground an urgent intervention to provide a temporary basic income for marginalized  and excluded women in Nepal in collaboration with the local government and conduct the feasibility  study on basic income for women in Nepal. The project contributes to the UN Nepal Framework for  Responding to the Socio-Economic Impacts of COVID. The initiatives undertaken under this project are  expected to inform and support the design of a full-fledged dedicated project reflecting the priorities  determined by the Feasibility Analysis, the priorities of the Government of Nepal, and the lesson learned  from the pilot initiative conducted in selected municipalities. The initiative is expected to provide  support to marginalized and excluded women in Nepal to cope with immediate survival needs and  support to become more economically empowered, informed and resilient to face the evolving COVID  context. The plan will be implemented by UNDP for 18 months.  Agreed

title: Promoting Green Recovery Project
description:
The Promoting Green Recovery Project (PGRP) is geared toward supporting COVID-19 recovery in Nepal. It works with various development partners to provide effective management of health care waste from hospitals to reduce the risk of COVID-19 transmission; support governments at the local level in effective management of municipal waste; and promote sustainable urban mobility through cycling campaign.

The project through UNDP’s Rapid Financing  facility in response to catalyze solutions to the pandemic through UNDP's "COVID 2.0" offer - Beyond Recovery: Towards 2030, prioritizes creating employment opportunities and fostering business recovery and green growth in the post-COVID context in line with UN Nepal Framework for Responding to the Socio-Economic Impacts of COVID-19. PGRP contributes to Sustainable Development Goals 1 (No Poverty), 3 (Good health and Well-being), 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), 12 (Responsible consumption and production), and 17 (Partnerships for The Goal).

title: COVID-19 Response and Recovery Support Project in Nepal
description:
Activity 1.1.1: Support local government with medical equipment and preventive gears in coordination with DCCMC

Activity 1.1.2: Risk messaging, awareness campaigns to raise awareness on COVID-19 and address the myths about COVID vaccination through different media platforms. (Govt approved messages)

Activity 1.2.1: Support government with vaccination program and the vaccination centres allocated by the government with focus on improving health facilities.

Activity 1.2.2: Rehabilitation/ establishment of handwashing stations, filtration units, waste management, Menstrual Health Management (MHM) at Schools, health facilities, isolation centres along with dissemination of relevant preventive messaging.

Activity 2.1.1: Most vulnerable households (especially girls, women and children with disability and children at risk) provided with value vouchers (NPR 13500 per household for 2 months) to support with their livelihood.

Activity 2.2.1: Disseminate protection related awareness messages through public service announcement and social behavioral change communication materials in various platforms.

Activity 3.1.1: In coordination with schools, provide relevant trainings to teachers on alternative mode of education, remote teaching and learning, and support schools to be functional.

Activity 3.2.1: Children provided with self-learning materials, alternative remedial classes and create an enabling learning environment at home and at school once it reopens, including minor school repairs.

description: his project aims to support Nepal in achieving the SDGs and the targets of 15th plan by creating enabling environment and capacity development through accelerated implementation. Inclusion is an integral part of this initiative as is the integration of poverty, environmental management and climate change: the new sustainable development agenda reflects a greater recognition of challenges arising from depleted natural capital, climate vulnerability, gender inequality, rural-urban migration and rising resource demands, all of which disproportionately affect the livelihoods and well-being of the poor and vulnerable. The project hence will mainstream gender and social inclusion throughout the project interventions.

title: Building Hope Along the Karnali River Basin (BHAKARI)
description:
Bhakari seeks to reach 22,350 households (117,750  people) in the six districts of Karnlai and Sudurpaschim province directly. This will be accomplished through three purposes: 

  1. increase household level food  access and availability.                     Key activities include; 
  • Forging partnerships with government and private actors to  improve access to input and output markets including linkages to agrovets, collection centers,  traders and information exchange platforms,
  • Vouchers for agricultural inputs and/ or small  livestock, and
  • Training and support for climate-smart perma-gardens.

2. improve access to sustainable water sources for productive purposes. Key activities inlcude;

  • Sustainable water infrastructure interventions focusing on  installation, management and maintenance of productive water projects, including multiple use water  systems, rainwater harvesting, irrigation storage and delivery systems,
  • Strengthening capacity for  functional, equitable and sustainable water management practices, and
  • 220+ Hardware Water  Projects. Productive Use Water Projects are a complementary activity designed to improve the food  security of communities.

3. reduce the impacts of natural disasters, with a cross-cutting purpose on increasing inclusion and  empowerment for marginalized groups. 

Key interventions will include 

  • Formation and mobilization of community first responder/  task force members
  • Risk assessment and planning, watershed level assessment and planning,  etc.,
  • Disaster risk mitigating structure, bio-engineering and fodder plantation, and (4)  Partnership with the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) to strengthen early  warning and weather information systems.

Other activities include;

  • Value-based food assistance, meeting 100% of macronutrient  requirements for one month plus other basic needs
  • Cash for work
  • Value-based  vouchers (for labor-poor households only), and Government Capacity Building in order to  better manage local emergency response and disaster funds.

Program activities will adhere to a Gender and Social  Inclusion (GESI) First approach.

title: Promoting Economic Resilience of COVID-19 Affected Vulnerable People  (PERCAV)
description:
Activity 1.1 Understanding the enterprise need of project participants for self-employment.

The project will conduct intersectional study which will provide the information on the most vulnerable groups present in the local government. Identification of project participants who will be engaged in self-employment (100% women and PWD) will be done as per the criteria specified in below section of beneficiary details. The assessment of areas of interest and knowhow of project participants towards self-employment will facilitate in designing the customized capacity building interventions for the participants. The process will ensure that the women and other marginalized groups are selected for economic empowerment.

 

Activity 1.2 Capacity building of project participants in entrepreneurship skill, enterprise development and marketing

The project will develop a short-term practical based Business Induction Package including customized MEDEP’s Start and Improve Your Business Modules, skills for business start-up, women in business, investment analysis, market analysis, access to finance and risks and its mitigation measures. A ToT will be given to staffs on the effective delivery of the Package. The trained project staffs will then conduct session with the project participants in the Package thereby capacitating them in entrepreneurship, enterprise development, and marketing.

 

Activity 1. 3 Conduction of training on technical skill-based training and providing necessary start-up support to project participants to operate the enterprise of their choice and knowhow.

The project participants will be provided with technical skill-based training to in the enterprise of their choice and knowhow and can include both on-farm and off-far enterprises such as poultry, tailoring, retail shops, restaurants, honey, non-timber products, pig farm, spice cultivation, goat rearing, vegetable farming, shoe making, handicraft etc. The training will be provided through relevant service providers. These trainees will later be supported with required materials and input support to start/strengthen their enterprises. Regular coaching and mentorship to the entrepreneurs will be done by project staffs for smooth start-up and guidance and motivation for successful operation which will provide them with income generation.

 

Activity 1.4 Facilitation in formalization of enterprises for greater access to investment

Facilitation will be provided for registration of the enterprise in relevant agencies. Further, linkages of entrepreneurs with financial institution, local government and Cottage and Small Industries Development Board will be done for resource leveraging. Similarly, the entrepreneurs will be supported in business plan development for obtaining financial loans. These will support entrepreneurs to greater access of resources, services, and finance.

 

Activity 1.5 Facilitation in integration of the enterprise’s product in the value chain

The entrepreneurs will be facilitated to get linked to their respective value chain actors for sourcing of input materials and market of their product. This will include linkages events with market actors, market visits by entrepreneurs, collective marketing, and market sensitization.

 

Activity 2.1 Strengthening leadership and decision-making skills of women entrepreneurs.

Development of a concise short-term (1 day) Agency-based Women Empowerment (AWE) package with be done with expert’s inputs. The AWE package will have content on self-realization, leadership, and decision-making skills. ToT on AWE will be provided to project staffs who will then conduct the AWE package session among the women entrepreneurs. This package will motivate the entrepreneurs on taking entrepreneurship roles and empower them in leadership and decision-making skills.

 

Activity 2.2 Sensitization of COVID preventive measures and gender equality among HHs of project participants by mobilization of women volunteers

Women volunteers such as Female Community Health Workers, Human Right Defenders will be engaged in sensitization of project participants household members in gender equality. ToT to women volunteers on gender sensitization and counselling sessions as well as COVID preventive measures to be delivered to participants household members will be done. After training, these trained women volunteers will go door to door of participants house and do the counselling to the family members on gender equality as well as COVID preventive measures. This intervention will support in greater realization on gaps in gender roles and motivate them to support each other.

 

Activity 2.3 Conduction of community gender awareness and GBV sensitization campaign

Mass campaigning can be an effective means to sensitize communities in gender equality and GBV issues. IEC materials including print materials, public service announcements, video messaging/digital stories will be developed and rights for broadcasting will be obtained. Disseminated will be through appropriate media including social media posts and radio stations. Similarly, Day Celebrations will be conducted in specific days. These events will support in sensitizing communities on gender equality and gender-based violence.

 

Activity 2.4 Advocate and facilitate LGs to have gender equality and social inclusion policies and programs

Policy mapping will be done that will allow to know the gap in gender equality and social inclusion related policies of LGs. Policy dialogue will be conducted with mobilization of women activists and DPOs for obtaining commitment in gender equality and inclusiveness by LGs. These LGs will be facilitated in development of gender and social inclusion policy (where not present) in consultation and inputs from women activists and DPOs. The endorsement and implementation of the policy by LGs will be a milestone in the area of GESI. Further, the facilitation in conduction of gender sensitive and inclusive budgeting workshop will be done. These events will support development and implementation of more inclusive programs that will have a long-term effect on GESI issues.

 

 

 

Activity 2.5 Strengthen the GBV control networks of LGs

The project will collaborate with local government to strengthen its GBV control networks. The local governments have provision of formation of GBV control networks at municipal and ward level, however, the formed networks needs more capacity building for active functioning. The project will held dialogue with district agencies for initiation in mobilization of these networks and support to provide the network members with trainings and necessary skills wherever needed to make the network functional so that it can serve the community effectively. The project will also work jointly with Judicial Committee of the LGs in capacity building of the committee members and strengthen the GBV fund wherever required. The women cell in respective LGs will also be supported to strengthen its functionality.

 

Activity 2.6 Provide targeted support including assistive devices to PWD

Disabled Peoples Organizations (DPOs) will be engaged to make assessment of PWD status in project areas. The assessment will provide the categorization of need-based support required for identified PWDs in working area. The project will provide targeted support to some of the most vulnerable PWDs.

 

Activity 3.1 Facilitate to develop economic recovery plan to address the impact of COVID-19 pandemic

LGs are provided with responsibility and authority to manage the COVID-19 pandemic. The project with inputs from experts, will facilitate LGs to come up with economic recovery plan to address the impact of the pandemic.  This plan will consist of various strategies including provision of stimulus package and food security through the dissemination of climate change adaptation technologies.

 

Activity 3.2 Collaborate with LGs to initiate establishment of community infrastructure

The project will collaborate with LGs to identify the need for community assets especially agriculture related infrastructure focusing on access to irrigation facilities and an agriculture resource centre. A joint fund with LGs will be created to invest in some of these collaborative initiatives on the establishment of identified community assets. These will provide necessary facilities to increase agricultural productivity that will support in  economic recovery.

 

Activity 3.3 Collaborate with LGs in emergency preparedness and response to stop the spread of COVID-19 infection

The project will collaborate with LGs and provide necessary PPEs and medical supplies to manage local isolation and health centres. This will support the LGs in better management of spread of COVID-19 infection.

title: Sustainable WASH for all
description:
Sustainable WASH for all, SUSWA, is a bi-lateral human rights progressive Water, Sanitation and Hygiene  project project funded by the Government of Nepal (GoN) and Government of Finland (GoF), as well as the European Union. The project is a continuation of financial and technical support that the GoF has been providing to the development of the WASH sector in Nepal since 1989.

SUSWA will be implemented through a period of five and half years, starting from Mid-November 2022. The project follows the fiscal calendar of Nepal.

The Project aim is to work in a total of 42 municipalities covering all ten districts of Karnali Province in western Nepal.

title: SASEC Highway Enhancement Project
description: The project road is a two-lane carriageway and carries about 14,000 vehicles per day. Traffic is forecast to reach 48,800 vehicles per day by 2041. The road will be median-divided and provides service lanes, footpath, and cycle lane in urban areas. Through the project, the road will be upgraded to a two-lane dual carriageway to accommodate the increasing traffic demand, with improved geometry, pavement, drainage, road safety, and climate- and disaster-resilient features. Grade separation or traffic signal will be adopted at junctions to improve safety for vulnerable road users including women and children who are more likely to walk, cycle or use public transport. River training and bank protection works will minimize the risk of erosion. The project design incorporates lessons from previous projects, including readiness, procurement, asset management and sustainability.

title: AGRATA: Advancing Green, Resilient and Accessible resources and Services for communities and Amplifying sustainability in Nepal.
description:
Goal: By 2028, as a result of DCA’s and partners’ works, most marginalized and vulnerable communities and their organisations are empowered, resilient and protected to claim their rights to participation and justice and have access to public and private sector services and resources.

Outcomes/ Objectives:

1. Communities affected by crisis are protected, have the resilience to prevent, withstand and recover from shocks.

2. Communities have adapted to climate change and resilient livelihoods, are included in green and sustainable food and market systems.

3. People know and claim human rights and basic freedoms and influence decisions affecting their everyday lives.

4. Staff enhanced capacity, adapted new technology and equipment, have resources, plans/policies/frameworks to implement the Project.

Outputs:

1.   Increased capacity of local humanitarian actors to lead preparedness and risk informed humanitarian actions.

2. Right holders have enhanced food security, livelihood options and agroecology system-based adaptation services.

3. Rights holders including EHRDs, and their groups and networks are capacitated to voice their concern and exercise their rights.

4. Duty Bearers including private sectors at the local and provincial level enhanced; allocate adequate resources; strengthen quality public services and formulate and implement inclusive Policy/programmes for economic empowerment, climate smart technologies, promote youth on DRR and CCA.

title: Implementation of Codex standards to support containment and reduction of foodborne AMR
description:
Activity 1.1 (G): Communication packages, case studies and outreach activities are developed to raise awareness of Codex standards, food safety and one health, and engage policy makers to support application of Codex standards, with a particular focus on the revised Code of Practice to minimize and contain foodborne AMR and the new Codex Guidelines on Integrated monitoring and Surveillance of Foodborne AMR, as examples of a One health approach.

Activity 1.2 (G) A series sustainable training programme, through the holding of several events and tutored courses, is developed to increase capacities at country level to understand and use Codex standards and collect and analyse data on the use and impact of Codex standards, with a particular focus on AMR.

Activity 1.3 (G): A mechanism to systematically collect and analyse data on the use of specified Codex standards and assess their impact is established, feeding into the M&E framework of the Global Action Plan on AMR.

Activity 1.4(G/R/C): A Global Tool to monitor implementation of AMR-relevant Codex standards into regional and national legislation is developed and piloted at the regional and national levels.

Activity 2.1 (G): A set of practical tools are developed to support Member countries in their efforts to apply the Codex Guidelines for integrated monitoring and surveillance of foodborne AMR and related standards.   

Activity 2.2 (R/C): A situation analysis and assessment of targeted countries’ surveillance capacities related to AMR is carried-out, using existing assessment tools (e.g.,FAO-ATLASS, etc.) and a plan for costed adjustments to the targeted countries' current surveillance system is provided, based on a collaborative, risk-based approach and in line with country needs.  

Activity 2.3 (R/C): Capacities for monitoring and surveillance systems of foodborne AMR in targeted countries, together with tools and guidance on establishment of such systems are strengthened (including reagents to perform AST/bacteriology). 

Activity 2.4 (R/C): Residue monitoring laboratory network is established to strengthen capacity for monitoring and surveillance systems of foodborne AMR in targeted countries.

Activity 2.5 (G): The operationalization of national surveillance networks is supported, including the capacity development and support to Members to collect submit data to InFARM.

Activity 3.1 (G): A set of practical tools are developed (including through the revision of practical guidelines and protocols being applied in countries), taking into account the most recent scientific developments, to provide Member countries with comprehensive resources to support their efforts to apply the relevant Codex standards such as the Code of Practice to minimize and contain foodborne AMR and related standards.  

Activity 3.2 (R/C): Targeted countries’ capacities are assessed using available tools (i.e., situation analysis; the progressive management Pathway tool on AMR - PMP) to identify their specific needs in relation to managing the risks posed by foodborne AMR, including through the review of policy and legal frameworks, the control functions, the interactions with stakeholders and the science and knowledge base. 

Activity 3.3 (R/C) Targeted countries are supported to adopt best practice in key areas of foodborne AMR based on existing tools and international guidance.

Activity 3.4 (R/C) Selected country’s Regulatory frameworks in the food and agriculture sector are assessed and strengthened, in line with the Codex COP to minimize and contain foodborne AMR, and other relevant Codex guidance.
